<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:dependency-refinement" data-paper-title="Dependency-Aware Trajectory Refinement for Efficient Multi-Turn Agent Fine-Tuning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-453bfd86cb2878fc">Does the auditable local DAG include an actual LLM dependency annotator?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adependency-refinement">Dependency-Aware Trajectory Refinement for Efficient Multi-Turn Agent Fine-Tuning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ShanghaiTech University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It prunes and merges a supplied fixture DAG to verify structure and rejection paths, not automatic semantic annotation. If input omits a key edge, pruning may legally drop a necessary turn. Compression ratios and mechanism passes are not agent fine-tuning quality or paper-level results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a fixture omits &#x27;the answer depends on turn two,&#x27; the pruner cannot infer the edge. Correct test graphs do not validate dependency extraction on open trajectories.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harness-bandit" data-paper-title="HarnessBandit: Joint Learnability-Transferability Scheduling for Multi-Harness Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-harness-bandit-ffd58529" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b961ccb8ddc0f357">Why might learning in one harness fail to improve performance under other interfaces?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharness-bandit">HarnessBandit: Joint Learnability-Transferability Scheduling for Multi-Harness Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology / Alibaba Cloud</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Tool protocols, prompts, and workflows change which states and actions are encountered. Some learning is specific to that organization. Harness Bandit allocates budget across harnesses for both learning and transfer. In-training gains are not cross-interface generalization; report evaluation conditions separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A model familiar with one edit command may face different arguments elsewhere. More practice on the known interface can improve its score without improving transfer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.13739">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.13739-harness-bandit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b961ccb8ddc0f357">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harness-bandit" data-paper-title="HarnessBandit: Joint Learnability-Transferability Scheduling for Multi-Harness Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ab71656976360ab1">Why schedule multi-harness training using both learnability and transferability?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharness-bandit">HarnessBandit: Joint Learnability-Transferability Scheduling for Multi-Harness Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology / Alibaba Cloud</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An easy harness may teach only its specific interface; a transferable but currently hard one may need exploration. Combining both signals and a bonus allocates limited budget and avoids overfitting to easy scores. Scheduling weights are training decisions; a reference function or multi-seed diagnostics are not cross-harness ability evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A provides many hints and B resembles deployment. Do not give A all budget for faster near-term gains without checking whether the learning transfers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.13739">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.13739-harness-bandit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ab71656976360ab1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harness-bandit" data-paper-title="HarnessBandit: Joint Learnability-Transferability Scheduling for Multi-Harness Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0750ff4e3195da29">What trade-offs distinguish uniform multi-harness allocation from bandit scheduling?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharness-bandit">HarnessBandit: Joint Learnability-Transferability Scheduling for Multi-Harness Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology / Alibaba Cloud</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Uniform allocation does not adapt to changing payoffs. A bandit can sample more from environments worth learning or uncertain at the current stage. It may favor short-term proxies and spend budget on exploration, so assess scheduling cost and transfer rather than only within-harness efficiency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After one harness saturates, shift budget to paths with transferable gains, while occasionally revisiting it to guard against stale estimates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.13739">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.13739-harness-bandit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0750ff4e3195da29">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harness-bandit" data-paper-title="HarnessBandit: Joint Learnability-Transferability Scheduling for Multi-Harness Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-2437ebba3b51eb5c">Do local online harness-selection counts establish completed multi-harness LLM RL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharness-bandit">HarnessBandit: Joint Learnability-Transferability Scheduling for Multi-Harness Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology / Alibaba Cloud</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The reference runs gates, allocation, and state updates, without real LLM RL, full rollouts, or transfer benchmarks. Synthetic learnability and transferability check weight response, not portable capability. Three-seed scheduling statistics cannot establish training effects.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>More allocations to an arm with a supplied high transfer score verify the scheduler. A manually set score does not measure model transfer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.13739">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.13739-harness-bandit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2437ebba3b51eb5c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:t1-terminal-rl" data-paper-title="T1: Terminal Agent Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-t1-terminal-rl-406c9b27" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b5ce8bc476b1bbed">Why must inference trajectories match optimizer examples when training large terminal agents?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3At1-terminal-rl">T1: Terminal Agent Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore / Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Terminal interactions include generated tokens, observations, and potentially changing execution paths. Reconstructed samples can optimize behavior that was never sampled. T1 keeps long rollouts traceably aligned with updates and supports scale. Record consistency is necessary for correct training, but does not establish capability or final gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If tool output sits between model turns and concatenation changes token boundaries, computed probabilities may no longer represent the original action.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11042">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.11042-t1-terminal-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b5ce8bc476b1bbed">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:t1-terminal-rl" data-paper-title="T1: Terminal Agent Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1063f6614633db4d">Why train on token IDs actually sampled in rollouts rather than retokenizing complete interaction text?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3At1-terminal-rl">T1: Terminal Agent Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore / Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Joining tool observations and turns before tokenization can alter boundaries or token IDs, so policy probabilities no longer correspond to sampled actions. TITO retains sampled IDs, boundary repair handles drift, and MoE route replay addresses expert-path differences. Alignment is a training contract, not evidence that terminal tasks were learned.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Concatenating a command and an observation can create different subtokens or include non-action content. Keep sampled IDs to align training with the original action.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11042">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.11042-t1-terminal-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1063f6614633db4d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:t1-terminal-rl" data-paper-title="T1: Terminal Agent Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1dad37cdd9124676">How does MoE route replay differ from replaying generated tokens alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3At1-terminal-rl">T1: Terminal Agent Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore / Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Expert routes may differ for identical tokens because of implementation or state. R3 saves and replays routing choices to narrow execution-path mismatch between training and inference. Token equality is necessary but insufficient; route equality also does not guarantee task gains without real model and log-probability comparisons.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a token originally selects experts A and B but training recomputes A and C, outputs and gradients can change despite identical token IDs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11042">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.11042-t1-terminal-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1dad37cdd9124676">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:t1-terminal-rl" data-paper-title="T1: Terminal Agent Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-802e5687f7b00d55">Does a local exact-token/route audit cover training a 122B MoE?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3At1-terminal-rl">T1: Terminal Agent Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore / Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It checks sampled sequences and route replay contracts, without a 122B model, cloud sandboxes exceeding 300 turns, or full terminal RL. Log consistency does not demonstrate a smaller training–inference gap. Paper scores and gap measurements belong to the authors&#x27; real system, not fixtures with matching fields.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A fixture route array that replays element by element confirms indexing, not actual MoE dispatch or backpropagation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式或操作, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11042">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.11042-t1-terminal-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-802e5687f7b00d55">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:multi-harness-rl" data-paper-title="What Does Multi-Harness RL Learn? Credit Assignment and Portability in Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-multi-harness-rl-66c31df3" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c9a85584b1ebed7b">Why separate base-model capability from execution-interface effects in multi-harness RL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amulti-harness-rl">What Does Multi-Harness RL Learn? Credit Assignment and Portability in Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · New York University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Different prompts, tools, and workflows change success on the same task; grouping changes the meaning of rewards. Multi-Harness RL examines their effects on learning and transfer. If the base, tasks, or samples also change, attribution is difficult. Control trajectories and evaluation definitions instead of calling all cross-harness gains capability growth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One harness fills arguments automatically while another requires the model to fill them. Success differences may reflect interface help rather than base reasoning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04518">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.04518-multi-harness-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c9a85584b1ebed7b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:multi-harness-rl" data-paper-title="What Does Multi-Harness RL Learn? Credit Assignment and Portability in Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2cb0d51874f501b1">What confound is isolated by freezing task–harness trajectories and changing only advantage grouping?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amulti-harness-rl">What Does Multi-Harness RL Learn? Credit Assignment and Portability in Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · New York University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Multi-harness training changes both data diversity and credit comparison groups. Comparing complete systems confounds them. Fixed trajectories let within-task comparison of cross-harness and within-harness normalization more directly test grouping. Report transfer differences and uncertainty on unseen minimal harnesses.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reuse trajectories for one repair task under two interfaces and recompute grouped advantages without resampling. This reduces attribution of sampling changes to the credit rule.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04518">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.04518-multi-harness-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2cb0d51874f501b1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:multi-harness-rl" data-paper-title="What Does Multi-Harness RL Learn? Credit Assignment and Portability in Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ed1a599911375548">How do Within and Cross change the relative meaning of the same reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amulti-harness-rl">What Does Multi-Harness RL Learn? Credit Assignment and Portability in Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · New York University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Within normalizes inside each task–harness group, comparing sibling trajectories in one environment. Cross normalizes across harnesses for the same task, including between-environment reward differences in advantages. It can learn environment preferences; portability needs paired tests on an unseen minimal harness, not just training means.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A stronger-tool harness can earn generally positive Cross advantages because its rewards are higher. That does not imply better code repair on a minimal interface.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04518">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.04518-multi-harness-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ed1a599911375548">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:multi-harness-rl" data-paper-title="What Does Multi-Harness RL Learn? Credit Assignment and Portability in Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f053cdb0bfd492e6">Why does a held-out Cross−Within interval spanning zero fail to establish transfer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amulti-harness-rl">What Does Multi-Harness RL Learn? Credit Assignment and Portability in Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · New York University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A small positive point estimate is still compatible with no change; interpret the paper alongside its paired confidence interval. Old local gold-reading scores are invalid. Current checks cover grouping, gradients, and protocols, without Qwen RL, actual coding harnesses, or a sealed oracle. Counts are not SWE-bench capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A 0.25 percentage-point gain with negative values inside the interval does not establish reliable superiority over Within. Do not omit the interval and report only the positive estimate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04518">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.04518-multi-harness-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f053cdb0bfd492e6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ace-data" data-paper-title="What Makes Good Agentic Data? An ACE Lens on Data Generation for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-ace-data-9a8b6ddd" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5a5ac4e33413cea3">Why does ACE say more agent trajectories do not necessarily make better training data?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aace-data">What Makes Good Agentic Data? An ACE Lens on Data Generation for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Trajectories may be incorrect, too hard for the learner, or repetitive, and more data can amplify those issues. ACE selects for Accuracy, Complexity, and Diversity to account for quality and learner fit. Define and evaluate each empirically rather than inferring benefits from more steps or topics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A thousand copies of an incorrect tool call are not good data. Many simple tasks the learner has mastered may also teach little.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27260">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.27260-ace-data/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5a5ac4e33413cea3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ace-data" data-paper-title="What Makes Good Agentic Data? An ACE Lens on Data Generation for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c709cf44b82a6aa7">Why must Complexity be calibrated to a specific learner instead of assigning a universal difficulty label?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aace-data">What Makes Good Agentic Data? An ACE Lens on Data Generation for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Learnability differs across models. Very easy examples add little signal and very hard ones may only generate failures. Accuracy first ensures credible samples, learner-relative complexity finds a useful band, and Diversity adds environment and behavior coverage. All three matter; length and tool count do not establish better data.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A novice can learn from three-step tool tasks and fail every twenty-step one. A stronger model may need the latter, so the curriculum band should depend on the learner.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27260">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.27260-ace-data/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c709cf44b82a6aa7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ace-data" data-paper-title="What Makes Good Agentic Data? An ACE Lens on Data Generation for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4ec1c6af15d90cb9">Why keep Complexity as learner challenge and Diversity as coverage separate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aace-data">What Makes Good Agentic Data? An ACE Lens on Data Generation for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Complexity measures difficulty for the specified learner; Diversity measures differences among samples and coverage of task space. Diverse data can be easy and difficult data can repeat one pattern. Both require Accuracy: a novel but wrong trajectory is not good supervision, and static labels do not establish training benefit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Ten different tools used once each offer broad but easy coverage. Ten similar hard error cases challenge the learner but cover a narrow area.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27260">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.27260-ace-data/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4ec1c6af15d90cb9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ace-data" data-paper-title="What Makes Good Agentic Data? An ACE Lens on Data Generation for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4855db385496d579">How does public artifact evaluation prevent three-stage admission from becoming fictitious training results?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aace-data">What Makes Good Agentic Data? An ACE Lens on Data Generation for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pin an actual dataset revision; record environments, questions, trajectories, verifier, and learner loss. Compare random and three-stage selection under equal budgets. The local path has admission contracts and artifact replay, not trained checkpoints or SOTA claims. Do not fill missing provenance or failures with synthetic high scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A JSONL export that passes field checks is an auditable input. Without training and independent model evaluation, it cannot show an ACE success-rate gain.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27260">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.27260-ace-data/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4855db385496d579">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:spo-plus-plus" data-paper-title="SPO++: Stabilizing Asynchronous Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Measure-Theoretic Token Correction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-spo-plus-plus-c1491ed7" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-67629927643b2cac">Why can asynchronous agent RL depend on which task finishes first?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aspo-plus-plus">SPO++: Stabilizing Asynchronous Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Measure-Theoretic Token Correction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Renmin University of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Long tasks have variable durations, so asynchronous training uses results as they arrive. Completion order can correlate with difficulty and policy version. SPO++ keeps throughput while aligning advantage baselines and statistics with the correct generation events. Fast completion is not representativeness; track sampling-time conditions rather than backfilling from later outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Easy tasks may return early and change historical values. A hard task dispatched earlier should not be treated as sampled with that new baseline.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24870">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.24870-spo-plus-plus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-67629927643b2cac">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:spo-plus-plus" data-paper-title="SPO++: Stabilizing Asynchronous Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Measure-Theoretic Token Correction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-12fbffeabf99f50b">Why weight advantage standardization by action-token count for a token-mean actor loss?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aspo-plus-plus">SPO++: Stabilizing Asynchronous Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Measure-Theoretic Token Correction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Renmin University of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Equal trajectory votes during whitening conflict with token-mean loss and change how long and short rollouts influence updates. Token weighting aligns normalization with the optimization measure. Freezing the baseline at dispatch prevents completion-order leakage; it is separate from redefining rewards by text length.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A 100-token trace occupies more loss positions than a 10-token trace. Giving them one vote each in normalization would mismatch actual gradient averaging.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24870">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.24870-spo-plus-plus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-12fbffeabf99f50b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:spo-plus-plus" data-paper-title="SPO++: Stabilizing Asynchronous Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Measure-Theoretic Token Correction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3c83d8cdc2ba5e67">What changes between freezing a baseline at dispatch and using the latest baseline at completion?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aspo-plus-plus">SPO++: Stabilizing Asynchronous Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Measure-Theoretic Token Correction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Renmin University of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Freezing associates each rollout with prompt value visible when dispatched. The newest value at completion incorporates later arrivals, affecting rollouts differently by duration. SPO++ indexes evidence by generation-policy events, so later history cannot override frozen conditions. This correction is independent of token-weighted standardization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A goes out before B but finishes after it. B can update future baselines without retroactively entering A&#x27;s dispatch-time history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24870">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.24870-spo-plus-plus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3c83d8cdc2ba5e67">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:spo-plus-plus" data-paper-title="SPO++: Stabilizing Asynchronous Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Measure-Theoretic Token Correction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-de233a30a2539d90">Do local event-time and token-measure checks include asynchronous Qwen training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aspo-plus-plus">SPO++: Stabilizing Asynchronous Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Measure-Theoretic Token Correction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Renmin University of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. A deterministic mini-suite checks frozen values, history timing, and action-token weighting, without real asynchronous models, ALFWorld, or Math-TIR. Event counts verify branches, not paper reward-curve area or throughput gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Out-of-order completion of ten fixtures tests timing, not real worker latency, policy staleness, or parameter updates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24870">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.24870-spo-plus-plus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-de233a30a2539d90">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ahead" data-paper-title="AHEAD: Agentic Hints for Effective Agent Development" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-ahead-17c82764" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d7aa07df3793e0b8">Why does AHEAD want more than one success or failure signal across an entire long-horizon agent trajectory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aahead">AHEAD: Agentic Hints for Effective Agent Development</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AWS AI Labs / Purdue University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A few critical errors may determine the outcome, while other steps are reasonable or merely affected by them. Uniform credit cannot identify what to fix. AHEAD uses targeted teacher signals to adjust learning on those steps. Fine-grained credit depends on error localization, and privileged teacher information is not available to the deployed agent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If only the third retrieval query strays, later failure should not assign equal responsibility to every correct evidence collection step.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24114">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.24114-ahead/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d7aa07df3793e0b8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ahead" data-paper-title="AHEAD: Agentic Hints for Effective Agent Development" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b9c59b738ccefc35">Why give a corrective hint only to the teacher on critical error steps instead of sharing full answers at every step?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aahead">AHEAD: Agentic Hints for Effective Agent Development</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AWS AI Labs / Purdue University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Ordinary steps already get environment feedback. Blanket privileged hints waste signal and hide where correction matters. After locating an error, compare log probabilities for the same generated action with and without the hint, then adjust terminal advantage within bounds. Hints stay on the training teacher side and cannot enter deployment student context.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If only the third step chooses the wrong tool, target that choice. Letting every step see the final solution is not autonomous completion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24114">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.24114-ahead/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b9c59b738ccefc35">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ahead" data-paper-title="AHEAD: Agentic Hints for Effective Agent Development" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e93dbc6554977b2b">How does multiplying the original episode advantage differ from using the teacher gap as a new reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aahead">AHEAD: Agentic Hints for Effective Agent Development</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AWS AI Labs / Purdue University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Multiplication modulates the original advantage within clip and λ limits, preserving the terminal signal. Replacement would turn teacher preferences into a separate objective. The gap is a likelihood difference for the same token in two contexts, not success probability or causal contribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A hint&#x27;s stronger support for a token in a failed trajectory does not unconditionally reward it as success; original advantage and the bounded factor still apply.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24114">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.24114-ahead/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e93dbc6554977b2b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ahead" data-paper-title="AHEAD: Agentic Hints for Effective Agent Development" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8331787f806cc0e1">How do deterministic local error locations, real ToolRoute, and the paper&#x27;s LLM analyzer differ?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aahead">AHEAD: Agentic Hints for Effective Agent Development</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AWS AI Labs / Purdue University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The mini-suite uses deterministic positions to test hint routing, with no LLM analyzer, Qwen GRPO, or three original benchmarks. ToolRoute is a different isolated feedback protocol, not complete algorithm training. Hints, gold, and reference actions stay in permitted training contexts and are not visible to the test policy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A fixture that identifies step six as wrong tests gating, not autonomous localization of that step in a real long failure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24114">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.24114-ahead/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8331787f806cc0e1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:autosaddler" data-paper-title="AutoSaddler: Automatic Harness Optimization with Durable Updates from Agent Execution Traces" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-autosaddler-3e805f29" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-311080cb265d3c16">Why does AutoSaddler turn one task&#x27;s failures into workflow improvements usable later?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aautosaddler">AutoSaddler: Automatic Harness Optimization with Durable Updates from Agent Execution Traces</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft / POSTECH</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Prompt, tool configuration, and middleware flaws can repeatedly cause long-task failures. Fixing one answer does not address shared causes. AutoSaddler proposes bounded harness edits from execution evidence and maintains persistent versions. Only execution validation and later reuse show a patch&#x27;s effect; version counts are not capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Repeatedly skipping pre-submission tests suggests a shared workflow change. Manually testing the current task fixes one deliverable, not future omissions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23041">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.23041-autosaddler/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-311080cb265d3c16">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:autosaddler" data-paper-title="AutoSaddler: Automatic Harness Optimization with Durable Updates from Agent Execution Traces" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-829d316001b1c096">Why select patches on a development set and record EvoDAG after a same-batch check?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aautosaddler">AutoSaddler: Automatic Harness Optimization with Durable Updates from Agent Execution Traces</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft / POSTECH</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The original failures help diagnose direction but can be overfit by a targeted patch. Recompare on development data; the version graph records parent harness and evidence for future iteration and rollback. Bounded structured patches do not imply semantic safety, and final reporting tests cannot choose updates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After fixing three identical errors, check other development tasks for regressions and save the parent–child relation instead of overwriting the only harness file.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23041">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.23041-autosaddler/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-829d316001b1c096">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:autosaddler" data-paper-title="AutoSaddler: Automatic Harness Optimization with Durable Updates from Agent Execution Traces" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1064a26346ac437f">Which persistent state changes when editing harness code versus base-model weights?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aautosaddler">AutoSaddler: Automatic Harness Optimization with Durable Updates from Agent Execution Traces</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft / POSTECH</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Harness edits change how prompts, tool configuration, or middleware organize later execution. Weight updates change the model&#x27;s behavior distribution. AutoSaddler iterates on the harness as a persistent code asset; workflow repair is not model training. The approaches can complement one another but require separate evidence, versions, and rollback targets.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A recovery branch after failed tests changes workflow code. If the checkpoint is unchanged, its parameters have not learned error recovery.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:autosaddler" data-paper-title="AutoSaddler: Automatic Harness Optimization with Durable Updates from Agent Execution Traces" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5f24efb3681d1296">What do local durable-update and reuse counts establish?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aautosaddler">AutoSaddler: Automatic Harness Optimization with Durable Updates from Agent Execution Traces</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft / POSTECH</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They show that the optimization loop, validation gate, and persistent reuse state run on a public mini-suite, without original GAIA2, SWE-Bench Pro, Terminal-Bench, or production harnesses. Diagnostic and write counts are not real LLM diagnosis, and proxy cost is not API cost, human efficiency, or online benefit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Twelve rule updates and 108 reuses verify the version path. Without real models and tools, the authors&#x27; nine-to-ten-point gain does not carry over.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-g2" data-paper-title="Agent-G²: Gaussian Guidance for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-agent-g2-1fe5ec6c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9bb87fa93054b0b0">Why does Agent-G² provide partial expert trajectories before exploration rather than relying only on random trial and error?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-g2">Agent-G²: Gaussian Guidance for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An expert prefix brings the policy to a state with more learning value, then the current policy explores from there. Existing rollouts estimate guidance proportions by difficulty cluster, balancing help with autonomy and avoiding costly per-example probes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A hard task can receive a longer start, while the policy takes over earlier on an easy task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23318">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.23318-agent-g2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9bb87fa93054b0b0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-g2" data-paper-title="Agent-G²: Gaussian Guidance for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6889355ac6f32e8c">Why sample guidance depth by difficulty cluster rather than retain the same expert-prefix length for every task?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-g2">Agent-G²: Gaussian Guidance for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Too much prefix on easy tasks reduces independent exploration; too little on difficult tasks can produce only failures. Cluster success rates and variability from existing rollouts set the center and variance of a guidance band, then depths are sampled per task, avoiding extra per-item probes. Training prefixes are scaffolding and must not be provided in independent evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An easy door task may need a very short hint; a complex multiroom task can need a longer start. Giving both half a prefix can overguide one and underguide the other.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23318">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.23318-agent-g2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6889355ac6f32e8c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-g2" data-paper-title="Agent-G²: Gaussian Guidance for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-70610fe508fd57ba">How does cluster-level guidance-band estimation differ in cost from repeated per-task probes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-g2">Agent-G²: Gaussian Guidance for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Clusters reuse success rates and variation from existing policy rollouts, reducing extra per-task trials. Individual probes can be finer but cost additional rollouts. Neither fixed nor cluster-based help establishes optimal depth for each task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Similar tasks can share a depth distribution rather than repeatedly testing every task to find a starting point.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23318">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.23318-agent-g2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-70610fe508fd57ba">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-g2" data-paper-title="Agent-G²: Gaussian Guidance for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e4661243a36cc425">What does Agent-G² do if it samples a negative guidance depth or a proportion beyond the expert trajectory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-g2">Agent-G²: Gaussian Guidance for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Bound the mean and clip Gaussian samples to [0,1], with a variance floor. Expert prefixes are training guidance; the hidden expert plan must not be supplied to policies in independent capability evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Clip r=1.2 to 1 rather than indexing past the trajectory or treating overflow as extra oracle information.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23318">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.23318-agent-g2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e4661243a36cc425">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:auso" data-paper-title="AUSO: Action-Level Unified Skill Optimization from Internalization to Utilization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-auso-a7af1bb4" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4d23c8a96e53e3ca">Why does AUSO both internalize skills and retain an action-level skill utilization stage?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aauso">AUSO: Action-Level Unified Skill Optimization from Internalization to Utilization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Retrieving external skills costs context, but fully internalized skills are harder to select per task. AUSO first uses skill-conditioned teachers for general internalization, then explores and compares action distributions with and without skills to adjust learning emphasis.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Common steps can be learned into the policy while a complex action may still benefit from a particular skill hint.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21292">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.21292-auso/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4d23c8a96e53e3ca">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:auso" data-paper-title="AUSO: Action-Level Unified Skill Optimization from Internalization to Utilization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-229676a9ebe02981">Why bound action-level JSD weighting and preserve the original trajectory advantage&#x27;s sign?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aauso">AUSO: Action-Level Unified Skill Optimization from Internalization to Utilization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Distribution differences with and without skills show action sensitivity, not whether the action benefited. Preserve the outcome-advantage sign so local weights only adjust credit magnitude and a highly divergent step in a failed trace does not become positive reward. Separate internalization, exploration, and utilization to reduce persistent external skill-context costs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If an action in a failed run heavily depends on a skill, it can receive stronger corrective learning, not a success reward merely for depending on that skill.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21292">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.21292-auso/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-229676a9ebe02981">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:auso" data-paper-title="AUSO: Action-Level Unified Skill Optimization from Internalization to Utilization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0132b36c11bbbdf1">Do AUSO&#x27;s action-level JSD and whole-trajectory success tell us the same thing?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aauso">AUSO: Action-Level Unified Skill Optimization from Internalization to Utilization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Success describes the outcome of the whole process. Action-level differences show a particular step&#x27;s sensitivity to skill conditioning. A large JSD does not establish causal benefit; combine it with outcomes and bounded weighting rather than equating divergence with improvement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Only one tool choice in a successful trajectory may really be affected by the skill.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21292">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.21292-auso/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0132b36c11bbbdf1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:auso" data-paper-title="AUSO: Action-Level Unified Skill Optimization from Internalization to Utilization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d5de36efbae3b19f">Why compare skill-conditioned and unconditioned policies at the same h_t and action-distribution granularity?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aauso">AUSO: Action-Level Unified Skill Optimization from Internalization to Utilization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Changing other context confounds JSD. Compare the distributions at the same action boundary, and verify that actual w is nonnegative and bounded. Writing 1±β alone does not ensure the advantage sign is preserved.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If one distribution sees a tool result and the other does not, the difference cannot be attributed only to skill S.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21292">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.21292-auso/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d5de36efbae3b19f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sapo" data-paper-title="SAPO: Single-Rollout Autoregressive Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-sapo-b38c3177" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-87217be71f41ec4d">Why does SAPO use one autoregressive backbone for policy and value?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asapo">SAPO: Single-Rollout Autoregressive Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiamen University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A shared backbone reads action decisions and value signals at different causal positions and combines PPO, on-policy SARSA, and trajectory GAE. Sharing parameters does not erase the different input boundaries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Policy information available before action generation and later information permitted for value estimates must follow the protocol separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19842">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.19842-sapo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-87217be71f41ec4d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sapo" data-paper-title="SAPO: Single-Rollout Autoregressive Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-de81b8c4f559f15f">Why specify different causal boundaries when one autoregressive backbone outputs both policy and value?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asapo">SAPO: Single-Rollout Autoregressive Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiamen University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Action probabilities use only visible history before the decision, and value estimates must match the correct time. Post-action observations can leak future information into advantages. A shared backbone saves structure, but PPO, SARSA, and GAE still need state/action alignment; a single rollout does not remove bootstrap and termination semantics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The value before a command cannot already see the command&#x27;s passing test result. Such credit would be precise only because the future leaked.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19842">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.19842-sapo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-de81b8c4f559f15f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sapo" data-paper-title="SAPO: Single-Rollout Autoregressive Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-31317deb3033a79a">How does single-rollout optimization differ from sampling many branches at one state for group comparisons?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asapo">SAPO: Single-Rollout Autoregressive Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiamen University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>SAPO organizes policy, value, and temporal advantage from a single on-policy trajectory. Branch-group comparison needs multiple rollouts. Data requirements, value estimation, and credit assignment differ, regardless of whether final success rates match.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An executed trajectory does not give the actual returns of untried alternatives at the same state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19842">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.19842-sapo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-31317deb3033a79a">Question link</a></p>
