</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sapo" data-paper-title="SAPO: Single-Rollout Autoregressive Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-218946eb5ef436a0">Why retain trajectory boundaries when calculating GAE instead of concatenating episodes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asapo">SAPO: Single-Rollout Autoregressive Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiamen University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Advantages accumulate later TD residuals. Concatenating episodes would propagate another task&#x27;s rewards into the current one. Respect terminal boundaries for bootstrapping and accumulation. The deterministic local mini-suite is not a browser run or full RL training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The first record after task A ends belongs to B and is not A&#x27;s future reward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19842">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.19842-sapo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-218946eb5ef436a0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:spade" data-paper-title="SPADE: Self-Play in Adaptive Synthetic Executable Environments" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-spade-5fdace60" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8d3ed730866d322d">Why does SPADE use the same LLM as environment designer and inference agent?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aspade">SPADE: Self-Play in Adaptive Synthetic Executable Environments</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The designer creates executable synthetic environments, the agent tries them, and the difference between hinted and unhinted rewards identifies frontier tasks. The aim is learnable challenges rather than arbitrary unsolvable problems.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An environment that fails without hints but succeeds with them may be more informative than one that fails both conditions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19197">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.19197-spade/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8d3ed730866d322d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:spade" data-paper-title="SPADE: Self-Play in Adaptive Synthetic Executable Environments" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c7c3a5bda0319f3a">Why use hinted versus unhinted regret for the environment designer rather than simply maximizing agent failure?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aspade">SPADE: Self-Play in Adaptive Synthetic Executable Environments</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Failure alone can reward impossible or overly hard environments. A hint that substantially improves a difficult unhinted outcome identifies a more learnable frontier. Environments must still execute, and privileged information stays in training comparisons rather than leaking into unhinted evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A difficult maze solvable with direction hints can be useful. A maze with no exit fails both agents and should not score well just for being hard.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19197">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.19197-spade/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c7c3a5bda0319f3a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:spade" data-paper-title="SPADE: Self-Play in Adaptive Synthetic Executable Environments" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a01da2b026001f3b">Do maximizing failure rate and maximizing hint/no-hint regret favor the same environments?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aspade">SPADE: Self-Play in Adaptive Synthetic Executable Environments</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Failure alone can favor unsolvable or meaningless environments. Regret also requires privileged help to improve return, distinguishing solvable but currently difficult tasks. It still needs real execution and feedback rather than a fixed difficulty label.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An environment that scores zero for both agents has a high failure rate but zero regret.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19197">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.19197-spade/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a01da2b026001f3b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:spade" data-paper-title="SPADE: Self-Play in Adaptive Synthetic Executable Environments" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-fe52868b4be336c7">May a SPADE agent retain hints in the no-hint evaluation condition?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aspade">SPADE: Self-Play in Adaptive Synthetic Executable Environments</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Isolate condition inputs. Privileged hints belong only to their training or comparison branch and must not enter the unhinted policy. Executable environment checks still matter; the local mini-suite did not run original external environments or large-model training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If an unhinted callback still receives the designer&#x27;s saved plan, the return difference cannot be interpreted.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19197">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.19197-spade/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fe52868b4be336c7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rtpo" data-paper-title="RTPO: Reverse-Turn Policy Optimization for Stabilizing Agentic RL Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-rtpo-1c108353" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-52f37824bda763dd">Why does RTPO organize multi-turn decisions into reverse updates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Artpo">RTPO: Reverse-Turn Policy Optimization for Stabilizing Agentic RL Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Adelaide University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Early action value depends on downstream continuation. RTPO arranges rollouts in a sparse reverse tree and updates turns backward to keep decisions aligned with the downstream policy evaluating them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Handle the consequences of late actions first, then return to earlier decisions rather than treating the trajectory as unstructured text.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.18682">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.18682-rtpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-52f37824bda763dd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rtpo" data-paper-title="RTPO: Reverse-Turn Policy Optimization for Stabilizing Agentic RL Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9c34e4b512e67b3c">Why do reverse-turn updates help keep decisions aligned with on-policy downstream continuations?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Artpo">RTPO: Reverse-Turn Policy Optimization for Stabilizing Agentic RL Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Adelaide University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Early action value depends on later policies. If downstream behavior has changed substantially, credit from old continuations can be inconsistent. A reverse tree handles turns near the outcome first, then propagates evidence backward so early decisions reflect the updated continuation. Update order does not remove importance or execution-alignment checks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After the last two steps learn recovery, assess opening decisions using that new recovery ability instead of values from the old failing continuation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.18682">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.18682-rtpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9c34e4b512e67b3c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rtpo" data-paper-title="RTPO: Reverse-Turn Policy Optimization for Stabilizing Agentic RL Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d0b1be0b8eafd96b">Are reverse-turn updates the same as training on reversed token text?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Artpo">RTPO: Reverse-Turn Policy Optimization for Stabilizing Agentic RL Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Adelaide University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Reverse order applies to decision updates and continuation dependencies. Causal language-model input still follows the legal trajectory. Reversing text changes the task and visibility and cannot substitute for reverse policy optimization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Updating turn three before turn two does not mean reading turn-three observations to predict a turn-one action.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.18682">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.18682-rtpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d0b1be0b8eafd96b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rtpo" data-paper-title="RTPO: Reverse-Turn Policy Optimization for Stabilizing Agentic RL Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-dd588ecabba448b1">Why record both behavior policy and downstream continuation version for each RTPO turn?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Artpo">RTPO: Reverse-Turn Policy Optimization for Stabilizing Agentic RL Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Adelaide University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Early advantages based on mismatched later policies can lose on-policy correspondence. Reversing indices alone is insufficient: check tree nodes, state, and continuation ownership. Local control flow is not complete external-environment RL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After a node is reevaluated under a new continuation policy, its old continuation reward is not the current return for the same state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.18682">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.18682-rtpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dd588ecabba448b1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:planpo" data-paper-title="PlanPO: Group Planning-Aware Policy Optimization for Multi-Turn Agentic LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-planpo-5fac2579" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-224fcadb29af723f">Why does PlanPO split planning efficiency into turn count and response length per turn?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aplanpo">PlanPO: Group Planning-Aware Policy Optimization for Multi-Turn Agentic LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiamen University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fewer environment interactions and shorter generated responses are distinct costs. PlanPO compares successes coarse-to-fine and combines efficiency with outcome advantage, retaining completion while improving the process.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two successful traces can differ in tool calls and explanation length; evaluate those dimensions separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.17289">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.17289-planpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-224fcadb29af723f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:planpo" data-paper-title="PlanPO: Group Planning-Aware Policy Optimization for Multi-Turn Agentic LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2c01413b29f93499">Why compare turn counts and response lengths only among successful traces rather than rewarding every short trace?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aplanpo">PlanPO: Group Planning-Aware Policy Optimization for Multi-Turn Agentic LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiamen University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Short can mean efficient planning or premature abandonment. First separate successes by outcome, then compare turns and response length among comparable successes. Coarse-to-fine advantages supplement outcome, not correctness, and fewer tokens cannot excuse skipped evidence collection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two successful bug fixes can differ by three wasted searches. A shorter trace that declares completion without editing files should get no efficiency reward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.17289">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.17289-planpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2c01413b29f93499">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:planpo" data-paper-title="PlanPO: Group Planning-Aware Policy Optimization for Multi-Turn Agentic LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-724afe0ef4b5ce66">How does PlanPO efficiency among successes differ from rewarding the shortest answer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aplanpo">PlanPO: Group Planning-Aware Policy Optimization for Multi-Turn Agentic LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiamen University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A direct length reward can favor failure or early stopping. Comparing successful traces first requires completion, then optimizes turns and length. Length advantage is not global outcome advantage and must remain separate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An unexecuted one-line &#x27;done&#x27; should not beat a successful multi-turn execution just because it is short.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.17289">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.17289-planpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-724afe0ef4b5ce66">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:planpo" data-paper-title="PlanPO: Group Planning-Aware Policy Optimization for Multi-Turn Agentic LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ce24322d0dd67bb6">Why distinguish agent responses from environment observations when counting turns and response lengths?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aplanpo">PlanPO: Group Planning-Aware Policy Optimization for Multi-Turn Agentic LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiamen University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The two axes measure interaction turns and per-turn generation. Counting long tool returns as agent output changes credit. Record success filtering, counting boundaries, and each advantage coefficient, not just total mean tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A tool can return a long page without the agent generating the same number of tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.17289">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.17289-planpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ce24322d0dd67bb6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:trca" data-paper-title="TRCA: Transition-wise Rubric Credit Assignment for Long-horizon LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-trca-ae92667a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-873192fd9718233f">Why does TRCA define a rubric for every state transition rather than scoring only the outcome?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atrca">TRCA: Transition-wise Rubric Credit Assignment for Long-horizon LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Terminal outcomes hide important actions. Transition rubrics separately check evidence, execution, and invalid behavior and add breakthrough rewards. They do not require a successful anchor and supply more detailed credit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A step can gather key evidence while failing execution, with separate scores rather than zeroing both.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16156">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.16156-trca/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-873192fd9718233f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:trca" data-paper-title="TRCA: Transition-wise Rubric Credit Assignment for Long-horizon LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-92f4d424dd06d08a">Why score Evidence, Execution, and Invalidity separately instead of one process score?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atrca">TRCA: Transition-wise Rubric Credit Assignment for Long-horizon LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A transition can add evidence but fail to execute, or be well formed without advancing the task. Rubric components distinguish those cases and penalize invalid behavior. Breakthrough credit identifies key progress without a successful anchor, but still needs actual transitions, not fixed template scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A search can reveal an error cause, followed by a command syntax failure. A total score alone obscures whether retrieval or invocation needs fixing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16156">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.16156-trca/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-92f4d424dd06d08a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:trca" data-paper-title="TRCA: Transition-wise Rubric Credit Assignment for Long-horizon LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0b6075a31659322e">How does TRCA&#x27;s lack of a success anchor differ from feedback that needs a successful reference trace?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atrca">TRCA: Transition-wise Rubric Credit Assignment for Long-horizon LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reference-based approaches first need a comparable successful execution. TRCA derives base and breakthrough rewards from actual transition rubrics without first finding a success. This is a feedback prerequisite, not proof of a higher task-success rate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Even when both full traces fail, a transition can collect useful evidence and receive rubric feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16156">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.16156-trca/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0b6075a31659322e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:trca" data-paper-title="TRCA: Transition-wise Rubric Credit Assignment for Long-horizon LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f234aa5e56240844">Why verify the sign and component logs when aggregating TRCA invalidity?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atrca">TRCA: Transition-wise Rubric Credit Assignment for Long-horizon LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Subtract r_invalid and add the other base and breakthrough terms as defined. Missing the negative sign rewards invalid behavior. Keep component scores linked to transitions, since a total can conceal mistakes. Fixed values are not real evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With other terms fixed, increasing invalidity must lower total reward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16156">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.16156-trca/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f234aa5e56240844">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sinkflex-rl" data-paper-title="Efficient Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tool-Use Agentic Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-sinkflex-rl-6bf5fe2a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1aa103458d0f49d2">Why does SinkFlex-RL address both rollout environments and attention memory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asinkflex-rl">Efficient Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tool-Use Agentic Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Capital One AI Foundations</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Long tool traces require multi-turn state management and face context and training-memory bottlenecks. It combines environments, fresh trajectory groups, value-model-free GRPO, and sink-aware FlexAttention, not just a compressed mask.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Saving attention memory still requires correct environment state for actual multi-turn policy updates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10357">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.10357-sinkflex-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1aa103458d0f49d2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sinkflex-rl" data-paper-title="Efficient Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tool-Use Agentic Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-10d9b7593d872e71">Why preserve model-specific sink scaling when using a sliding-window or causal mask?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asinkflex-rl">Efficient Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tool-Use Agentic Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Capital One AI Foundations</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sparse visibility and sink scaling affect different parts of attention. Mask changes do not justify dropping the model&#x27;s scaling. Training still needs real environment state, long context, and GRPO data flow; a passing formula or kernel is not full on-policy rollout and tool-task verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the window retains recent text and sink but also removes special sink scaling, output changes combine two interventions and cannot be attributed to the window alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10357">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.10357-sinkflex-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-10d9b7593d872e71">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sinkflex-rl" data-paper-title="Efficient Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tool-Use Agentic Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-eb11358bd9590099">How do GRPO group-relative advantage and PPO with an independent value model differ in training dependencies?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asinkflex-rl">Efficient Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tool-Use Agentic Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Capital One AI Foundations</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>This approach builds relative advantages from groups without a separate value model, then applies a clipped policy objective and KL regularization. Changing advantage estimation alters rollout and memory needs; it is not an optimizer name change.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Grouped returns provide a relative baseline, not a trained per-state critic.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10357">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.10357-sinkflex-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eb11358bd9590099">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sinkflex-rl" data-paper-title="Efficient Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tool-Use Agentic Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-065d32c7060b868a">Why not replace SinkFlex-RL token averaging with per-trajectory averaging and equal weights?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asinkflex-rl">Efficient Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tool-Use Agentic Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Capital One AI Foundations</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The denominator is total valid length ΣT_i, giving long and short trajectories a different weighting from equal per-trajectory means. Preserve model sink scaling and verify the actual mask. The local mini-suite does not reproduce FlexAttention GPU memory curves.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Trajectories of lengths 10 and 100 contribute differently to the token mean than to a mean with half the weight each.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10357">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.10357-sinkflex-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-065d32c7060b868a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:residency-rl" data-paper-title="ResidencyRL: Reinforcement Learning in Simulated Clinical Environments" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-residency-rl-21b2b4df" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e23450ebdaeb526a">Why does ResidencyRL use multi-turn simulation instead of only static knowledge questions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aresidency-rl">ResidencyRL: Reinforcement Learning in Simulated Clinical Environments</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Active inquiry, tool use, and long-horizon decisions need observed interaction effects. The method connects scenario generation, information-asymmetric environments, isolated multidimensional judges, and GRPO to train an interactive policy rather than memorizing answers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The agent must decide what to ask next from new observations rather than receiving all hidden scenario information up front.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.07418v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.07418-residency-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e23450ebdaeb526a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:residency-rl" data-paper-title="ResidencyRL: Reinforcement Learning in Simulated Clinical Environments" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2ea7561e68c91b4a">Why keep hidden references on the environment and judge side in simulations with asymmetric information?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aresidency-rl">ResidencyRL: Reinforcement Learning in Simulated Clinical Environments</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The policy must gather evidence through questions, tools, and observations. Direct reference access bypasses long-horizon decision making. Isolate scoring dimensions before aggregation to reduce contamination, but the reward formula is not the full environment or professional capability. Local diagnostics are not clinical efficacy or decision reliability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a state should be revealed only after querying it, do not provide the reference summary in the policy prompt and call the result autonomous evidence collection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.07418v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.07418-residency-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2ea7561e68c91b4a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:residency-rl" data-paper-title="ResidencyRL: Reinforcement Learning in Simulated Clinical Environments" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e206b051f6ef2513">How does aggregating six reward dimensions differ from implementing the full simulation training algorithm?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aresidency-rl">ResidencyRL: Reinforcement Learning in Simulated Clinical Environments</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Aggregation combines already obtained normalized scores and penalties. The method also requires scenarios, actual interactions, separate judges, and policy updates. Fixed scores or a loss wrapper cannot replace that chain.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Combining six numbers into R does not establish that the model performed and learned from a simulated interaction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.07418v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.07418-residency-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e206b051f6ef2513">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:residency-rl" data-paper-title="ResidencyRL: Reinforcement Learning in Simulated Clinical Environments" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d22abfba171c8915">Why cap the ResidencyRL penalty with min(3,P) rather than arbitrarily clipping total reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aresidency-rl">ResidencyRL: Reinforcement Learning in Simulated Clinical Environments</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>First calculate three times the weighted normalized dimension scores, then subtract a penalty capped at three. Preserve order and the distinct terms. Hidden scenario information is for the environment and judges; isolated judge calls must not pass the reference to the policy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Increasing P from 4 to 10 still deducts 3; it does not change the other dimensions&#x27; scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.07418v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.07418-residency-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d22abfba171c8915">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:envace" data-paper-title="EnvACE" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-envace-95e34f1b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a38fc9fc88352019">Why does EnvACE switch the same policy into a rehearsal role?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aenvace">EnvACE</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It predicts the next observation between real actions, performing limited private look-ahead without a separately trained world model. Training constrains acting and rehearsal; a planning prediction is not a tool execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The agent imagines a likely response before deciding whether to take the action.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06197">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.06197-envace/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a38fc9fc88352019">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:envace" data-paper-title="EnvACE" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-50472467ca29dd53">Why compute group-relative advantages separately for acting and rehearsal?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aenvace">EnvACE</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Action success and observation-prediction rewards have different scales and objectives. Centering them together lets one role&#x27;s high scores suppress the other&#x27;s learning. Separate groups let the shared policy learn environment prediction and plan with private rehearsal. Imagined observations are not tool feedback or execution evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A high score for predicting an open door should not mistakenly reward a failed real action; keep rehearsal distinct from the actual tool result.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06197">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.06197-envace/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-50472467ca29dd53">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:envace" data-paper-title="EnvACE" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2e2c2fb84e75f438">How does same-policy rehearsal differ architecturally from a separate world model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aenvace">EnvACE</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Rehearsal reuses the agent policy under a role condition. An independent world model has its own prediction model and training and maintenance costs. Reuse does not guarantee accuracy: keep imagined observations and real feedback separate and compute role advantages separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>&#x27;The tool may succeed&#x27; from rehearsal is not a successful tool return.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06197">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.06197-envace/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2e2c2fb84e75f438">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:envace" data-paper-title="EnvACE" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5bc4bf2059fbd6c1">Why exclude rehearsal predictions from EnvACE&#x27;s real tool-response count?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aenvace">EnvACE</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Counting them would disguise imagination as execution evidence. The documented mini-suite has real_tool_responses=0; rehearsal and role-wise updates establish those paths, not browser or real-tool success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Three predicted observations are three rehearsals, not three actual API calls.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06197">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.06197-envace/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5bc4bf2059fbd6c1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cipo" data-paper-title="Contextual Information Policy Optimization for Search Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-cipo-5f899139" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0323829fb5f31cf8">Why does CIPO add evidence credit to intermediate search steps?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acipo">Contextual Information Policy Optimization for Search Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Final answer reward does not show whether retrieval affected decisions and may encourage confirming prior beliefs. CIPO credits later action changes informed by external evidence and combines dense credit with global outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Revising a plan after finding counterevidence is more informative than appending an irrelevant citation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06128">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.06128-cipo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0323829fb5f31cf8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cipo" data-paper-title="Contextual Information Policy Optimization for Search Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-fca80e0fca779969">Why can terminal answer rewards foster confirmation bias, and how does dense evidence credit help?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acipo">Contextual Information Policy Optimization for Search Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The model may guess first and retrieve only supporting information, with an accidentally correct answer hiding poor search. Credit turns where external evidence changes later actions to reward use of information rather than call counts. Keep global outcomes so novelty does not divert attention from the question.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a search disproves a guessed date and the agent checks another source, distinguish that evidence-driven change from repeating the original guess.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06128">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.06128-cipo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fca80e0fca779969">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cipo" data-paper-title="Contextual Information Policy Optimization for Search Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-bd6a60f81287a8df">How does CIPO evidence-impact credit differ from rewarding citation counts?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acipo">Contextual Information Policy Optimization for Search Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Citation counts measure surface form. Evidence credit concerns whether external information affects later actions. Seeing retrieved text alone does not establish causal influence; verify it under the method&#x27;s definition.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Ten links that change nothing may be less useful than one piece of evidence that changes a decision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06128">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.06128-cipo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bd6a60f81287a8df">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cipo" data-paper-title="Contextual Information Policy Optimization for Search Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ef7fbb791d5bdef3">Which advantage remains at the λ=0 and λ=1 boundaries in CIPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acipo">Contextual Information Policy Optimization for Search Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>λ=0 uses only outcome and λ=1 only evidence, checking the mixing direction. Intermediate values combine them. Bind turn credit to real trajectory positions, and do not replace local mini-suite results with the paper&#x27;s large-model scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If evidence still changes updates at λ=0, check coefficients or a leftover branch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06128">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.06128-cipo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ef7fbb791d5bdef3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-opsd" data-paper-title="AgentOPSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-agent-opsd-6c6325b8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-edd89b34aa8c5592">Why does AgentOPSD use turn evidence to update success belief recursively?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-opsd">AgentOPSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Trajectory rewards do not identify key decisions. Aggregate teacher/student token log-probability gaps from privileged replay by turn, accumulate them in log odds, and assign local credit from successive belief changes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A tool choice that sharply raises belief is easier to localize from the change than from an already high level.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05987">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.05987-agent-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-edd89b34aa8c5592">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-opsd" data-paper-title="AgentOPSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-79e8ecd371a73695">Why identify pivotal turns from changes between adjacent success beliefs rather than the final belief?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-opsd">AgentOPSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The final value mixes all prior evidence and cannot localize the decisive turn. Accumulate teacher–student token probability differences in log odds and use the per-turn sigmoid belief increment to identify a local change. This is hindsight attribution for training; privileged replay and references stay out of independent evaluation policies.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a tool response causes belief to jump after several uneventful steps, its increment identifies the turn better than broadcasting a high final belief.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05987">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.05987-agent-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-79e8ecd371a73695">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-opsd" data-paper-title="AgentOPSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ae5b7f23496958c6">Does critic-free AgentOPSD require no teacher information?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-opsd">AgentOPSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It has no independent value critic, but turn evidence still uses teacher/student differences in privileged replay. Mini-suite state updates do not establish actual large-model teacher rollouts and policy training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>No critic network does not remove the teacher distribution required for e_t.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05987">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.05987-agent-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ae5b7f23496958c6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-opsd" data-paper-title="AgentOPSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3a8ec969cbfd98ea">Why accumulate AgentOPSD evidence in log odds and take sigmoid differences?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-opsd">AgentOPSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Update log-odds state ℓ_t=ℓ_{t−1}+e_t and credit the difference between adjacent sigmoid beliefs. Adding e_t directly to a probability can leave its range and changes accumulation. Compute large log odds stably, and keep privileged replay out of evaluation policy inputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The same e_t changes different prior beliefs by different amounts; it is not a fixed additive probability adjustment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05987">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.05987-agent-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3a8ec969cbfd98ea">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:state2state" data-paper-title="State2State: Environment-Derived Mid-Training for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-state2state-baaabd4d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7d9b8c2719a98f32">How does State2State construct training tasks automatically through environment exploration?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Astate2state">State2State: Environment-Derived Mid-Training for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University AIR / Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Exploration yields reachable initial and target states. A fixed projection T matches terminal state as the verifier, giving tasks without human-written descriptions or expert trajectories for every item. The policy still finds its own path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Knowing a room&#x27;s initial and target layouts does not identify the sequence of actions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04934">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.04934-state2state/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7d9b8c2719a98f32">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:state2state" data-paper-title="State2State: Environment-Derived Mid-Training for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-af6d87b1df83394d">Why can tasks built from initial and target states omit expert action trajectories?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Astate2state">State2State: Environment-Derived Mid-Training for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University AIR / Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The goal says where to arrive while the policy explores how. Rule-based state matching only verifies the endpoint, separating task generation from demonstrations and widening mid-training sources. Verifier-internal goals or rules are not stepwise correct-action hints. Matching must preserve task-relevant state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Given initial and target object layouts, the agent moves objects itself and the environment compares the result; it does not need a prescribed left-then-right sequence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04934">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.04934-state2state/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-af6d87b1df83394d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:state2state" data-paper-title="State2State: Environment-Derived Mid-Training for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-763bfc28ba021ee8">Does target-state supervision give the same information as behavior cloning from an expert?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Astate2state">State2State: Environment-Derived Mid-Training for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University AIR / Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A target state defines success; behavior cloning also provides the action sequence. Goal supervision permits multiple valid routes. Passing verifier-computed expert paths to the policy would invalidate the no-demonstration setting.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two different paths can both succeed by reaching the goal, without copying a canonical sequence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04934">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.04934-state2state/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-763bfc28ba021ee8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:state2state" data-paper-title="State2State: Environment-Derived Mid-Training for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a7a8506d6f99e52e">Why predefine the State2State projection in T(s_T)=T(s*)?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Astate2state">State2State: Environment-Derived Mid-Training for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University AIR / Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The projection determines which differences matter. Changing T after observing results changes the task. Verify initial and terminal states, legal transitions, and matching fields. A local state operator does not replace actual large-model mid-training in the paper&#x27;s environment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a goal specifies object positions, do not remove position from matching after a failure to manufacture success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04934">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.04934-state2state/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a7a8506d6f99e52e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ocsd" data-paper-title="OCSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-ocsd-b0061afd" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f363eb1521afa2c4">Why does OCSD worry that replay scaffolding itself changes token scores?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aocsd">OCSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Extra structure and prompt formatting during future-observation replay can affect predictions independently of the observation. Use structurally matched Full and Observation-Ablated controls to extract a residual better focused on the observation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A long replay template can change probabilities, so not every change comes from environmental evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04788">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.04788-ocsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f363eb1521afa2c4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ocsd" data-paper-title="OCSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7cac41cdba0e5c86">Why subtract structurally matched Observation-Ablated replay from Full replay?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aocsd">OCSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Comparing replay with future observations directly against the student conflates observation content and extra scaffolding. Keep the structure and remove only observations, then subtract to isolate information contribution better and amplify updates only on uncertain steps. Future information is for training attribution, not test-time input.</p>
