<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the replay template adds &#x27;please check,&#x27; keep it in both versions. Only observation availability should differ so the prompt effect is not counted as observation evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04788">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.04788-ocsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7cac41cdba0e5c86">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ocsd" data-paper-title="OCSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a3015dc1b5914cab">What does the Full–Ablated residual control for beyond the Full–Student gap?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aocsd">OCSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A single gap includes both observation content and scaffolding. A matched ablated condition removes the observation while preserving structure, so subtraction cancels shared effects. Unmatched templates leave new confounds.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If Full alone includes another instruction, Full−Ablated also captures that instruction&#x27;s effect.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04788">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.04788-ocsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a3015dc1b5914cab">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ocsd" data-paper-title="OCSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f927523ea57cddbb">How do the two student log probabilities cancel in the OCSD residual?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aocsd">OCSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>For the same token and student condition, r=(logπ_full−logπ_S)−(logπ_abl−logπ_S)=logπ_full−logπ_abl. If the student values come from different prefixes or alignments, fix matching before cancellation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Compare both expressions on the same input to detect sign or position mistakes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04788">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.04788-ocsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f927523ea57cddbb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:evoharness-rl" data-paper-title="EvoHarness-RL: Learning Self-Evolving Runtime Harness for Long-Horizon LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-evoharness-rl-68a7cfc6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-071696521e65d6fd">Why does EvoHarness-RL make runtime-state reads and writes trainable actions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aevoharness-rl">EvoHarness-RL: Learning Self-Evolving Runtime Harness for Long-Horizon LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana–Champaign / Meta AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>If fixed scripts maintain Belief, Progress, and Experience, the policy cannot learn when updates or merging are worthwhile. SFT teaches harness actions, then task rewards and costs train when to use them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A simple task may need few experience edits, while a long task benefits from saving intermediate progress.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05446">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.05446-evoharness-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-071696521e65d6fd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:evoharness-rl" data-paper-title="EvoHarness-RL: Learning Self-Evolving Runtime Harness for Long-Horizon LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f87d53ba6777d290">Why make Belief, Progress, and Experience external state the policy can read and write?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aevoharness-rl">EvoHarness-RL: Learning Self-Evolving Runtime Harness for Long-Horizon LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana–Champaign / Meta AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A fixed harness can make inappropriate decisions about storage and merging. Explicit actions teach the policy to manage belief, progress, and experience, using SFT to learn the interface and then optimizing task reward minus management cost. More writing is not inherently useful, and state must reflect actual observations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Write new constraints to Belief and merge duplicates into Experience. Appending every log each turn can consume more than the task gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05446">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.05446-evoharness-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f87d53ba6777d290">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:evoharness-rl" data-paper-title="EvoHarness-RL: Learning Self-Evolving Runtime Harness for Long-Horizon LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-da44087982608915">How does a learned harness policy differ from configuring fixed memory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aevoharness-rl">EvoHarness-RL: Learning Self-Evolving Runtime Harness for Long-Horizon LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana–Champaign / Meta AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A fixed module prescribes read/write behavior. A learned harness policy chooses when to read, write, or merge and pays operation costs. An &#x27;evolvable&#x27; registry label on a fixed pipeline does not establish learned external-state management.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Saving all history every turn is different from deciding whether to save based on current progress.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05446">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.05446-evoharness-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-da44087982608915">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:evoharness-rl" data-paper-title="EvoHarness-RL: Learning Self-Evolving Runtime Harness for Long-Horizon LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ac7fc64654335ad8">Why bind EvoHarness-RL&#x27;s harness cost to actual execution logs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aevoharness-rl">EvoHarness-RL: Learning Self-Evolving Runtime Harness for Long-Horizon LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana–Champaign / Meta AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>In R=R_task−λC_harness, cost must reflect executed reads, writes, and merges, not proposals alone. Check whether later policy steps read the updated state. The local mini-suite is not full paper-scale LLM RL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Text saying &#x27;merge experience&#x27; without a state update is not a successful harness action.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05446">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.05446-evoharness-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ac7fc64654335ad8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hindsearch" data-paper-title="HindSearch: Trajectory-Level Hindsight Critique for Search-Augmented Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-hindsearch-b112afa3" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-859ae4093ffa2212">Why does HindSearch generate hindsight critique after a failed search trace completes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahindsearch">HindSearch: Trajectory-Level Hindsight Critique for Search-Augmented Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Santa Clara University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Terminal success is sparse. A frozen judge can use gold to identify problems in a completed failure and supply auxiliary on-policy distillation signals. Hindsight explains training failures; it is not future answer information available during evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After training execution, note that search ignored key evidence to improve the next policy rather than answer the current test item.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01597">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.01597-hindsearch/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-859ae4093ffa2212">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hindsearch" data-paper-title="HindSearch: Trajectory-Level Hindsight Critique for Search-Augmented Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-412d450bc5952de0">If a judge can read gold to generate critiques, why can&#x27;t that critique be supplied directly during search evaluation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahindsearch">HindSearch: Trajectory-Level Hindsight Critique for Search-Augmented Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Santa Clara University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Gold helps the training judge explain failures and turn sparse outcomes into actionable distillation signals. A reference-derived critique for the same evaluation task indirectly discloses answer information, invalidating independent search. Freezing the judge does not remove privileges in its inputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Training feedback can use the correct date to identify a wrong source, but testing must provide only the question, not a critique revealing that Wednesday is correct.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01597">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.01597-hindsearch/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-412d450bc5952de0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hindsearch" data-paper-title="HindSearch: Trajectory-Level Hindsight Critique for Search-Augmented Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0822ca2bca11cec5">What does a trajectory-level hindsight critique add beyond binary success or failure values?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahindsearch">HindSearch: Trajectory-Level Hindsight Critique for Search-Augmented Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Santa Clara University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Critique can identify specific shortcomings and their relationships, while binary outcomes only show success. A teacher or judge produces it at a cost and may be wrong; longer explanations are not automatically more accurate supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two zero-scoring traces could reflect missing retrieval versus misread evidence, which a single zero does not distinguish.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01597">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.01597-hindsearch/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0822ca2bca11cec5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hindsearch" data-paper-title="HindSearch: Trajectory-Level Hindsight Critique for Search-Augmented Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0989636a7474d473">Who can read gold in HindSearch, and which inputs must stay out of independent search evaluation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahindsearch">HindSearch: Trajectory-Level Hindsight Critique for Search-Augmented Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Santa Clara University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Only the frozen training judge and independent scoring side get gold. Critique derived from it is privileged training feedback. The evaluated policy cannot receive the current item&#x27;s gold, judge object, or gold-derived hints without contaminating success rates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Placing a judge&#x27;s answer-based corrective suggestion in a test search prompt is not leakage-free inference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01597">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.01597-hindsearch/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0989636a7474d473">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tapo" data-paper-title="TAPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-tapo-abc37e08" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bff3209c0d122b62">Why does TAPO reuse observed environment transitions to add training signal?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atapo">TAPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A rollout contains each post-action observation as well as terminal reward. Predicting s_{t+1} from (s_t,a_t) teaches the shared backbone action consequences without additional expert demonstrations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Use actual tool responses to teach the model what feedback its actions produce.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27973">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.27973-tapo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bff3209c0d122b62">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tapo" data-paper-title="TAPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e6111f746314c1da">Why can learning next observations from reused rollouts add training signal without adding deployment inference steps?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atapo">TAPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each transition already has state, action, and next observation. An auxiliary prediction target on the shared backbone uses them without new expert or policy rollouts. Deployment keeps the original policy without explicitly calling a predictor. Controlled comparisons must establish task gains; predicting feedback does not imply choosing good actions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An ls command already returns a directory listing. Train transition prediction from it, but deploy the policy to choose commands without first imagining a listing at each step.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27973">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.27973-tapo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e6111f746314c1da">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tapo" data-paper-title="TAPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-70ad992f4cddf423">Is TAPO&#x27;s training-time transition prediction the same as an extra world-model call at deployment?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atapo">TAPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Its auxiliary objective trains a shared backbone without requiring extra prediction at deployment. Explicit world-model planning adds online calls. More training supervision need not add inference cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The model can learn next-observation prediction and still generate only the original action before using a tool.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27973">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.27973-tapo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-70ad992f4cddf423">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tapo" data-paper-title="TAPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-967576bf775d342b">Why check that s_t, a_t, and the next observation belong together in TAPO targets?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atapo">TAPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Misalignment or cross-episode concatenation supervises the wrong action result. Targets must come from legal feedback in the same rollout, without exposing s_{t+1} in prediction input. High mini-suite accuracy is not real tool modeling capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Step two should predict the third observation it caused, not the first observation in the next task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27973">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.27973-tapo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-967576bf775d342b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:grsd" data-paper-title="Group-Reflective Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-grsd-ed16d3df" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e89fb2bb2adfb023">Why does GRSD reflect on verified success and failure trajectories for the same task?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agrsd">Group-Reflective Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Terminal reward mixes useful behavior, repeated mistakes, and chance. Contrasting reflections within a task yields specific DO/AVOID guidance to modulate turn credit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Both trajectories retrieve information, but only one checks a key condition. The contrast helps isolate useful behavior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28076">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.28076-grsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e89fb2bb2adfb023">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:grsd" data-paper-title="Group-Reflective Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-97caf32fa0217ef6">Why generate DO/AVOID guidance with a stop-gradient snapshot and make it visible only during training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agrsd">Group-Reflective Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Guidance comes from verified same-task successes and failures. A frozen snapshot prevents the guidance path from drifting with current gradients. It modulates turn credit without leaking hindsight group outcomes to evaluation policies. Positive multipliers preserve outcome-advantage direction rather than making reflection an answer or reward oracle.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If successes check dependencies and failures edit directly, derive training guidance from that contrast. A new test task cannot receive reflections from its own future success and failure group.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28076">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.28076-grsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-97caf32fa0217ef6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:grsd" data-paper-title="Group-Reflective Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d2cc0c2d48d654f2">How does GRSD&#x27;s success/failure group comparison differ from copying one successful trajectory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agrsd">Group-Reflective Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A success can contain accidental or unnecessary steps. Group comparison uses failures to identify what to do or avoid. It is training guidance, not an oracle for independent testing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An irrelevant tool call in a successful trace is not automatically worth learning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28076">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.28076-grsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d2cc0c2d48d654f2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:grsd" data-paper-title="Group-Reflective Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0cf8f23b8cf80af1">Why check GRSD&#x27;s positive modulation m_t separately from outcome advantage?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agrsd">Group-Reflective Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>m_t&gt;0 adjusts magnitude while preserving the outcome advantage&#x27;s sign; a negative value reverses the update. A stop-gradient snapshot provides training-only guidance, which must not remain in evaluation inputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An action that should become less likely must still become less likely after multiplication by positive m.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28076">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.28076-grsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0cf8f23b8cf80af1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cast" data-paper-title="CAST" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-cast-0c2b025a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1dd56ca2824b7355">Why does CAST query a solver for values of adjacent states instead of relying only on final wins or losses?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acast">CAST</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Terminal signals cannot localize contributions in long games. Solver value before and after an action yields turn-level credit alongside outcome to indicate how each step changed the situation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A step can materially improve reachability before completion; its value difference supplies earlier feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25308">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.25308-cast/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1dd56ca2824b7355">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cast" data-paper-title="CAST" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0544eb1cba34b953">Why does a solver&#x27;s value difference between adjacent states complement rather than replace terminal outcomes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acast">CAST</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Value change provides local progress credit toward solvability and can identify important steps. Solver estimates can be imperfect and local improvement can end in failure, so retain outcome advantage as a global constraint. Any hidden answers available to the training-side solver must be isolated from evaluation actors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Simplifying constraints can earn positive local credit, but a later invalid result still makes the trajectory unsuccessful.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25308">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.25308-cast/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0544eb1cba34b953">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cast" data-paper-title="CAST" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1351945562a08193">Do solver state values and a learned policy value critic have the same source of supervision?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acast">CAST</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A solver computes values externally in a solvable environment, while a critic usually learns estimates from experience. Solvability and query costs constrain solvers; accuracy of a tiny shortest-path oracle does not generalize to arbitrary agent tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Exact solutions on small deterministic graphs do not imply a similarly cheap perfect solver exists for web tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25308">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.25308-cast/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1351945562a08193">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cast" data-paper-title="CAST" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-44cde34b2c4454d2">How does CAST avoid reversing states in V(s_{t+1})−V(s_t)?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acast">CAST</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Bind before and after states to the same action and use a consistent value direction. Reversing them records progress as negative credit. Count actual solver calls and keep training-side values from becoming a hidden-answer interface for evaluated policies.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A value change from 0.2 to 0.5 should give +0.3, not −0.3.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25308">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.25308-cast/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-44cde34b2c4454d2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:seed" data-paper-title="SEED" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-seed-34cb6214" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5ff13b56066ad7da">Why does SEED turn reflections on completed trajectories into reusable hindsight skills?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aseed">SEED</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reflections attached only to an answer do not accumulate as stable training signal. SEED extracts skills, compares probabilities for original actions with and without them, and combines dense distillation with outcome RL to reuse experience.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A failure can yield the skill &#x27;check tool preconditions first&#x27; as training guidance for later tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14777">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.14777-seed/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5ff13b56066ad7da">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:seed" data-paper-title="SEED" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-28ff13e83ba14c21">Why distill probability differences with and without hindsight skills on original actions instead of copying new expert traces?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aseed">SEED</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Skills come from completed-trajectory reflection. Compare conditional probabilities on states and actions actually visited by the student for denser local supervision. Hindsight explains original behavior without requiring a teacher to take another route. Deployment must not receive future answers for the same task, and skill mistakes can contaminate signals, requiring verification boundaries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the student checked a directory and reflection finds it useful, compare the probability of that same action with and without the skill rather than substituting a teacher&#x27;s command.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14777">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.14777-seed/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-28ff13e83ba14c21">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:seed" data-paper-title="SEED" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1b8702074452165b">How does SEED rescoring on original actions differ from letting a teacher generate a full successful trace?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aseed">SEED</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Rescoring keeps the actual student states and actions, measuring skill-conditioning changes. A new expert trace may visit different states. This is on-policy rescoring, not imitation of a separate ideal execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the student executed A, compare A in both conditions instead of replacing it with unexecuted B.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14777">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.14777-seed/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1b8702074452165b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:seed" data-paper-title="SEED" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-83fb8cee4148afc3">What alignment must remain fixed when calculating a SEED skill log-probability difference?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aseed">SEED</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use the same s_t, a_t, and policy evaluation convention, changing only skill conditioning z. Otherwise the gap includes state or action changes. Hindsight is training feedback; do not leak test-answer-derived skills into the policy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Scoring A with the skill and B without it does not measure the effect of skill guidance on A.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14777">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.14777-seed/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-83fb8cee4148afc3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:turn-opd" data-paper-title="TurnOPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-turn-opd-4aa539f6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d1e3ea105a700501">Why does TurnOPD study both rollout depth and within-turn supervision normalization?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aturn-opd">TurnOPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Academic author team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Later turns differ in training value and cost. Probes choose sampling depth, while turn-normalized KL changes supervision shares for long and short turns, separately controlling sampling budget and update weight.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Sampling fewer turns and reducing the relative weight of one long turn are distinct savings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.05804">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.05804-turn-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d1e3ea105a700501">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:turn-opd" data-paper-title="TurnOPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a39bbdba25423153">Why does normalizing KL by turn length change the training weight of long and short turns?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aturn-opd">TurnOPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Academic author team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Token sums naturally give long turns more loss, potentially drowning out short critical decisions. Turn-normalized supervision averages within a turn; separate probes allocate rollout depth to informative interactions under limited teacher budget. Weighting and sampling changes do not imply that deeper or greater supervision always helps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A key tool choice may be 10 tokens and an explanation 200. Turn averaging reduces the twentyfold weighting difference caused by length alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.05804">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.05804-turn-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a39bbdba25423153">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:turn-opd" data-paper-title="TurnOPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-dd0b137eb5166900">How do token-averaged KL and a sum of length-normalized turn KL differ in weighting?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aturn-opd">TurnOPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Academic author team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Token-level aggregation gives long turns more terms. Dividing each turn by its own length gives turns more comparable weights. The same token batch can still define different objectives.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A 100-token turn does not automatically get ten times the weight of a 10-token turn if both are first normalized separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.05804">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.05804-turn-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dd0b137eb5166900">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:turn-opd" data-paper-title="TurnOPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-76ebf6fc34171b93">After dynamic truncation, may TurnOPD retain teacher scores from omitted turns in the loss?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aturn-opd">TurnOPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Academic author team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Supervision must match actual cutoff L* and not use fictitious targets for uncollected turns. Respect valid response lengths. The current teacher is a deterministic task oracle, not a task-specific large model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If this rollout stops at turn three, prefabricated answers for turns four through six are not training evidence for it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.05804">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2607.05804-turn-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-76ebf6fc34171b93">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:steppo" data-paper-title="StepPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-steppo-4ceaabe2" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ee8199c6224d4965">Why does StepPO use observation–action as the natural decision unit?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asteppo">StepPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Tool actions span tokens while environment feedback follows the complete action. StepPO computes value and GAE at step boundaries and aggregates action-token ratios into a step ratio before clipping.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A tool call has a name and arguments, but the environment returns feedback only after the complete invocation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.18401">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2604.18401-steppo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ee8199c6224d4965">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:steppo" data-paper-title="StepPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-77600865a38c44dc">Why does StepPO aggregate token ratios within a step before clipping the step ratio?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asteppo">StepPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The environment executes a whole action, so independent token clipping differs from action-level probability change. Average within-step log ratios and exponentiate, then compute value and GAE at step boundaries, aligning credit with environment transitions. Exclude tool observations from action tokens and preserve consistent length normalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A shell command has many tokens but executes once when complete. Evaluate the step&#x27;s overall change rather than assigning its state reward independently to each subword.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.18401">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2604.18401-steppo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-77600865a38c44dc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:steppo" data-paper-title="StepPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-bb09405ae546c81a">Is clipping token ratios before averaging equivalent to aggregating and clipping a step ratio?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asteppo">StepPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Clipping is nonlinear, so order changes which actions are constrained. Average log ratios and exponentiate to obtain a geometric step ratio, not the arithmetic mean of raw ratios.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>For one large and one small ratio in an action, geometric aggregation can produce a different update from individual clipping.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.18401">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2604.18401-steppo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bb09405ae546c81a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:steppo" data-paper-title="StepPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4af94536ae2c6cbc">How does StepPO keep observation tokens out of action-ratio aggregation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asteppo">StepPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Mark step and response-token boundaries and aggregate only policy ratios of tokens in the action. Observations are conditions, not generated actions. Deterministic local tool plans verify a step state machine but not real LLM token rollouts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A thousand-character tool response must not become a thousand policy tokens in the action&#x27;s ratio mean.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.18401">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2604.18401-steppo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4af94536ae2c6cbc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:searl" data-paper-title="SEARL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-searl-fe3972b7" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-56cf2479bbb6356c">Why does SEARL store tool experience in a graph with successful transitions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asearl">SEARL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai AI Laboratory</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The graph represents relationships between tools and effective transitions for retrieval and policy decisions. New rollouts update edge weights and the policy, so experience changes with actual outcomes rather than remaining static.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Repeated success for one tool sequence can make that relationship easier to retrieve for later tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.07791">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2604.07791-searl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-56cf2479bbb6356c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:searl" data-paper-title="SEARL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4211ad26baa9dca9">Why update both graph memory and policy with new rollouts rather than freeze the tool graph?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asearl">SEARL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai AI Laboratory</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Executions reveal usable and failed tool transitions, which should change edge weights. The policy also learns to use updated relationships. Fixed graphs limit exploration to older experience, while updating the graph alone does not ensure consumption. Both sides need real rewards, not preset successful edges.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a tool&#x27;s output can newly feed another tool, adding the edge is not enough; the policy should learn to select that route.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.07791">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2604.07791-searl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4211ad26baa9dca9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:searl" data-paper-title="SEARL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-158bda47b868b306">How does SEARL&#x27;s joint graph and policy update differ from editing memory only?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asearl">SEARL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai AI Laboratory</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Graph changes alter retrieved external information. Joint updates also change how the policy uses it and acts. Training the policy with a fixed graph likewise misses experience structure evolution. Record both state histories separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A new successful edge does not show that policy parameters learned to use it in relevant states.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.07791">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2604.07791-searl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-158bda47b868b306">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:searl" data-paper-title="SEARL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-50efd1f955befd96">How can SEARL show later decisions actually consume graph updates rather than only logging writes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asearl">SEARL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai AI Laboratory</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compare edge weights before and after rollouts, later retrieval hits, and policy inputs to confirm that updated experience is available. Nonzero telemetry proves events, not real browsing or multi-GPU RL capability from the mini-suite.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If edge weights change on disk but the policy reads stale cache, the experience loop did not close.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.07791">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2604.07791-searl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-50efd1f955befd96">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:simula" data-paper-title="Reasoning-Driven Synthetic Data Generation and Evaluation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-simula-9d7ce82b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-43e969fdccf0f6d8">Why does Simula build a factor taxonomy before generating examples?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asimula">Reasoning-Driven Synthetic Data Generation and Evaluation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · EPFL</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Direct seed expansion can limit coverage and produce similar samples. A tree organizes factors and combinations; generation controls global node combinations and local scenarios before independent critique and relative complexity calibration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Separate task type, conditions, and difficulty factors before combining them into distinct cases instead of repeatedly rewording one item.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.29791">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2603.29791-simula/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-43e969fdccf0f6d8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:simula" data-paper-title="Reasoning-Driven Synthetic Data Generation and Evaluation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6dd6ff06e3e13093">Why aren&#x27;t correctness and incorrectness critiques just repeated versions of the same decision?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asimula">Reasoning-Driven Synthetic Data Generation and Evaluation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · EPFL</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A single critic may accept surface plausibility. Separately asking for evidence of correctness and looking for errors gives complementary filters. Admission requires satisfying requirements, positive correctness, and negative incorrectness judgments. Factor trees ensure coverage and batch-relative difficulty calibrates complexity; rule checks cannot replace semantic critiques as quality evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A polished question may contain mutually exclusive requirements. An error-seeking critic should uncover them rather than echoing &#x27;looks good.&#x27;</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.29791">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2603.29791-simula/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6dd6ff06e3e13093">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:simula" data-paper-title="Reasoning-Driven Synthetic Data Generation and Evaluation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-172bf44316db2ae0">How does Simula&#x27;s Elo-based relative complexity differ from absolute model-assigned difficulty?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asimula">Reasoning-Driven Synthetic Data Generation and Evaluation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · EPFL</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Elo updates within-batch rankings through pairwise outcomes and depends on matchups and settings. Absolute scores use a different scale. Local initial 1000, scale 400, and k=32 are explicit settings, not claimed as the authors&#x27; unique values.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Harder than other examples in this batch does not give a universal unit of difficulty across tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.29791">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2603.29791-simula/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-172bf44316db2ae0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:simula" data-paper-title="Reasoning-Driven Synthetic Data Generation and Evaluation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-42fd38ef1def93cd">If Simula&#x27;s two critics share a base model, may the second see the first verdict?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asimula">Reasoning-Driven Synthetic Data Generation and Evaluation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · EPFL</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Call independently with only the sample. Admission requires the requirements critic to pass, correct to affirm, and incorrect to deny. Semantic generation and critique are central; fixture callbacks or zero 13-gram overlap on short text do not establish full quality or absence of contamination.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Telling the error critic that the other critic already passed the sample breaks independence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议与调用边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.29791">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2603.29791-simula/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-42fd38ef1def93cd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:dmast" data-paper-title="Dual-Modality Multi-Stage Adversarial Safety Training: Robustifying Multimodal Web Agents Against Cross-Modal Attacks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-dmast-279d6cde" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b729efde757ea518">Why does DMAST share VLM parameters across agent and attacker roles?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Admast">Dual-Modality Multi-Stage Adversarial Safety Training: Robustifying Multimodal Web Agents Against Cross-Modal Attacks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Role conditioning supports interaction and self-play with shared parameters, so robustness training covers defense decisions and attack trajectories. The full method also uses teacher imitation and oracle-reasoning SFT; the Stage 3 reward formula is one part.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One base model generates both kinds of trajectories under different role prompts, not two independent policies.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.04364v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2603.04364-dmast/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b729efde757ea518">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:dmast" data-paper-title="Dual-Modality Multi-Stage Adversarial Safety Training: Robustifying Multimodal Web Agents Against Cross-Modal Attacks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8e05154677691641">Why calculate group mean and variance from raw rewards while applying successful-response length penalty only in the advantage numerator?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Admast">Dual-Modality Multi-Stage Adversarial Safety Training: Robustifying Multimodal Web Agents Against Cross-Modal Attacks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
