<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Length penalty modulates credit for one successful response, not the group&#x27;s baseline and scale. Attacked groups also combine raw attacker and defender returns. Penalizing before whitening changes their comparison and the algorithm. Exclude zero-variance groups rather than using arbitrary epsilon to manufacture signal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two equally successful responses differ in length. Penalize the longer advantage without letting extra text drag the common raw-return baseline.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.04364v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2603.04364-dmast/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8e05154677691641">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:dmast" data-paper-title="Dual-Modality Multi-Stage Adversarial Safety Training: Robustifying Multimodal Web Agents Against Cross-Modal Attacks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-389529b5addb5ba5">What is missing if only DMAST&#x27;s group-statistics objective is implemented?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Admast">Dual-Modality Multi-Stage Adversarial Safety Training: Robustifying Multimodal Web Agents Against Cross-Modal Attacks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It can verify loss and gradients. Full visual-agent adversarial training needs a real VLM, environment interaction, teacher imitation, oracle SFT, and self-play. A mathematical diagnostic generates no attack payload and does not establish browser success or robustness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One SGD step on a tiny policy cannot support the same capability claim as all training stages in an interactive environment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.04364v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2603.04364-dmast/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-389529b5addb5ba5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:dmast" data-paper-title="Dual-Modality Multi-Stage Adversarial Safety Training: Robustifying Multimodal Web Agents Against Cross-Modal Attacks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-70306168e069480f">Should DMAST&#x27;s training-to-sampling probability ratio multiply both PG and KL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Admast">Dual-Modality Multi-Stage Adversarial Safety Training: Robustifying Multimodal Web Agents Against Cross-Modal Attacks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Only PG receives min(π_old/π_sampling,1), and PG is zero if the ratio is below 0.1. KL is not scaled by that condition. Exclude zero-variance groups and normalize by all valid response tokens in the batch rather than averaging per role.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Dropping PG for a low-ratio token does not justify deleting its reference KL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.04364v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2603.04364-dmast/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-70306168e069480f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:pearl" data-paper-title="PEARL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-pearl-a555b8b4" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-929aae8a41b36595">Why does PEARL run offline tool trial and error before online planning?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apearl">PEARL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 中国科学院信息工程研究所</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Hallucinated tools and wrong arguments break multi-hop plans. Offline exploration collects tool usage and failure conditions, then online separates Planner and Executor so planning can use more reliable experience.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Learn required parameters and failure conditions before the Planner decides a call sequence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.20439">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2601.20439-pearl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-929aae8a41b36595">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:pearl" data-paper-title="PEARL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c63eec069a33caa8">Why jointly reward tool chains and outcomes even with separate Planner and Executor roles?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apearl">PEARL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 中国科学院信息工程研究所</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A well-formed plan does not ensure tools exist, order is executable, or the answer is correct. An executor can supply bad arguments despite a sound plan. Offline trial and error records usage and failures; dense online signals separately constrain tool choice, order, and result. A high process component is not actual success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Looking up an order before refunding is a correct sequence, but a wrong order ID still fails. Reward both chain quality and final outcome.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.20439">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2601.20439-pearl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c63eec069a33caa8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:pearl" data-paper-title="PEARL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-76d0171ea8615e7d">How does training feedback differ between decoupled Planner/Executor and one model thinking and calling tools as it goes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apearl">PEARL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 中国科学院信息工程研究所</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Decoupling can use tool choice, order, and final success as planning rewards while the Executor handles execution feedback. A good plan does not guarantee success: verify arguments and runtime effects.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A plan can pick all three tools correctly yet fail because the Executor supplies wrong arguments.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.20439">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2601.20439-pearl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-76d0171ea8615e7d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:pearl" data-paper-title="PEARL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b9c18c460dc7c583">Why retain PEARL tool/order/success components rather than only total reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apearl">PEARL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 中国科学院信息工程研究所</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each component measures tool identity, ordering, or completion, helping localize planning signals and check weight directions. A total hides defective components. Local exploration and reuse are not live ToolHop API calls or complete GRPO.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If tools are correct but ordered incorrectly, the order term should explain the lower reward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.20439">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2601.20439-pearl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b9c18c460dc7c583">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent0" data-paper-title="Agent0" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-agent0-bc007c7f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8d1f4c7bee308515">Why does Agent0 create a curriculum with a task generator and several execution agents?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent0">Agent0</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Verifiable tasks create training opportunities automatically, multiple candidates give group feedback, and difficulty rises with the capability frontier. Zero human data does not mean no success criteria; the verifier still constrains curriculum quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After executors master a task family, propose a slightly harder but still verifiable task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.16043">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2511.16043-agent0/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8d1f4c7bee308515">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent0" data-paper-title="Agent0" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-67c36df868cd6ab4">Why must task verifiers check majority votes rather than treating agreement as truth?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent0">Agent0</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Executors may share wrong assumptions. Voting measures agreement, not independent factual correctness. External task rules verify candidates, and curricula advance near the current ability boundary. If the generator or voter sees references, leakage invalidates claims of autonomous tool capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Five executors can agree on the same wrong unit conversion. A verifier uses the task contract, not the number of votes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.16043">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2511.16043-agent0/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-67c36df868cd6ab4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent0" data-paper-title="Agent0" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1054f5b756fea842">Do agent majority agreement and independent verifier acceptance provide the same evidence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent0">Agent0</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Agreement checks whether candidates match; verification checks task satisfaction. Shared errors can win a vote. Candidate groups cannot prove themselves correct, and agreement alone cannot establish improvement for curriculum advancement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Five identical wrong results still agree, but the verifier should mark failure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.16043">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2511.16043-agent0/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1054f5b756fea842">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent0" data-paper-title="Agent0" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ae86237122a8fe2d">Can Agent0&#x27;s verifier return its internal solution or gold answer directly to executors?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent0">Agent0</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Execution and evaluation inputs should contain public task conditions only; hidden references stay with the verifier. Check task executability and feedback provenance. Saturated mini-suite success cannot establish LLM self-evolution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the generator hides a canonical action sequence in the execution prompt, success no longer establishes autonomous solving.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.16043">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2511.16043-agent0/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ae86237122a8fe2d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-r1" data-paper-title="Agent-R1" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-agent-r1-da1f3512" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-62f2c79ffa3c825e">Why does Agent-R1 record each agent–environment interaction separately?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-r1">Agent-R1</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A transition links state, action, and next observation for pluggable context management and environments, plus selectable token- or step-level credit. It is more structured than one text example containing the whole chat.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A tool call and its return form a distinct training record.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.14460">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2511.14460-agent-r1/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-62f2c79ffa3c825e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-r1" data-paper-title="Agent-R1" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8a55f93cba02dd89">Why do independent interaction transitions help switch between token-level and step-level credit?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-r1">Agent-R1</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They explicitly preserve state, action, and next-observation boundaries, enabling attribution at generated-token or environment-step granularity instead of flattening the transcript. Pluggable context management cannot change transition semantics. Tool output stays an environmental observation, not a policy action loss term merely because it is logged together.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A query can return a long table and still be one action. Assign step credit or split credit only among tokens that generated the query.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.14460">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2511.14460-agent-r1/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8a55f93cba02dd89">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-r1" data-paper-title="Agent-R1" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-24b67c242f79eb7d">Are token-level and step-level credit just two loss names?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-r1">Agent-R1</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Decision units, value boundaries, and action-length treatment differ. Explicit transitions make choices auditable. Renaming the optimizer does not fix confused observation and policy-response boundaries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A tool action with 20 tokens is one environment step, not 20 pieces of environment feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.14460">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2511.14460-agent-r1/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-24b67c242f79eb7d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-r1" data-paper-title="Agent-R1" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9d3ce2876478b905">How do Agent-R1 transition logs prevent the next observation from becoming visible to the current action?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-r1">Agent-R1</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Keep temporal boundaries among s_t, a_t, and o_{t+1}; generating a_t cannot read o_{t+1}. Cut advantage recurrence at episode termination. Local mechanism updates are not actual multi-GPU agent training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Before a tool call, policy input cannot already contain its future response.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.14460">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2511.14460-agent-r1/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9d3ce2876478b905">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mua-rl" data-paper-title="MUA-RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-mua-rl-ac5031c4" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6064a2872b370dfe">Why does MUA-RL include the user in dynamic rollouts instead of using only an initial request?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amua-rl">MUA-RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Real users can clarify or change intent, requiring the policy to adjust tool actions. The method interacts with simulated users and learns from final completion rather than treating user input as static.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A new constraint in turn two should change later tool arguments.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.18669">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2508.18669-mua-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6064a2872b370dfe">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mua-rl" data-paper-title="MUA-RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-09abb6a40a03acf3">Why exclude simulated-user messages from agent policy-token loss just like tool responses?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amua-rl">MUA-RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They are produced by the environment&#x27;s user policy or tools, not chosen by the agent. Supervising them confuses actions with conditions. Dynamic users support clarification and changing requirements, but final reward should measure completion rather than imitation of simulated user text. Simulation does not cover all real behavior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a user changes the date to Friday, the agent should reschedule, not learn to generate the user&#x27;s phrase &#x27;move it to Friday&#x27; itself.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.18669">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2508.18669-mua-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-09abb6a40a03acf3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mua-rl" data-paper-title="MUA-RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b0003b8f82cef21c">What differs between dynamic user simulation and tool results as the only environmental feedback?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amua-rl">MUA-RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>User messages can change or clarify goals; tool results mainly report post-action state. Both are environment inputs with different roles. Static tool traces cannot cover policies for evolving requests.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A tool can report success and a user clarify that they wanted a different outcome; the agent still needs to understand the request.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.18669">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2508.18669-mua-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b0003b8f82cef21c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mua-rl" data-paper-title="MUA-RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-bef8d360a271edc5">Can the MUA-RL simulated user expose the scenario&#x27;s complete hidden goal directly?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amua-rl">MUA-RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Only reveal what a user could say under the interaction protocol, not private references or the entire solution. Loss covers agent responses only. A deterministic local user and mini tools are not an external LLM or production database.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The user can reveal a constraint after clarification rather than attaching the full canonical tool sequence at the beginning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.18669">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2508.18669-mua-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bef8d360a271edc5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-lightning" data-paper-title="Agent Lightning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-agent-lightning-78a73390" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-dc5ea5ae4caba782">Why does Agent Lightning first convert execution events into common transitions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-lightning">Agent Lightning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Agent runtimes log differently. Common MDP transitions and credit decomposition let training interpret states, actions, and rewards independently of execution, not just store logs elsewhere.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A failed test after a code edit should connect to that patch action and state, not remain an isolated log message.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.03680">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2508.03680-agent-lightning/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dc5ea5ae4caba782">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-lightning" data-paper-title="Agent Lightning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9eae2b8c915b5c27">Why is separating training and execution more than storing logs on a different machine?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-lightning">Agent Lightning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A common transition contract converts framework behavior into attributable MDP data for return and advantage calculation, while execution keeps its tool orchestration. Missing state/action boundaries or mixed environment tokens prevent correct updates despite physical separation. Decoupling alone does not establish improvement for any agent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A trainer can update from standardized query actions and results. An unsegmented chat transcript is not directly an action sequence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.03680">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2508.03680-agent-lightning/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9eae2b8c915b5c27">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-lightning" data-paper-title="Agent Lightning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d90a4c4e3c50b51e">How does execution/training decoupling differ from asynchronously collecting logs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-lightning">Agent Lightning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Decoupling also maps traces into trainable transitions, assigns credit, and sends updated policies back to execution. Asynchronous logging only records and transmits. Without an execution path consuming updates, the loop is not connected.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Growing logs while every subsequent run uses an unchanged policy does not let training affect execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.03680">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2508.03680-agent-lightning/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d90a4c4e3c50b51e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-lightning" data-paper-title="Agent Lightning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-677f718873b61e65">Which policy does the local Agent Lightning update using real test rewards?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-lightning">Agent Lightning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The code sandbox uses test exit codes to credit patches, updates a bounded patch policy, and reuses it by bug family. It does not run LightningRL on LLM parameters. Check command, edit, and test events separately from rewards and memory use.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Failed tests can change later patch choices without updating LLM weights with RL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.03680">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2508.03680-agent-lightning/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-677f718873b61e65">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:webagent-r1" data-paper-title="WebAgent-R1" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-webagent-r1-938cd977" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e697ddfc76e544bd">Why does WebAgent-R1 train on complete multi-turn web trajectories?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Awebagent-r1">WebAgent-R1</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Virginia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>State, HTML, and action history change during interaction, and success depends on multiple decisions. The method manages recent and relevant context dynamically, collects full traces, and updates from group-relative outcomes instead of optimizing isolated answers repeatedly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After clicking to a new page, choose the next action from the new state, not the initial page.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.16421">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2505.16421-webagent-r1/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e697ddfc76e544bd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:webagent-r1" data-paper-title="WebAgent-R1" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-be6d569f718d3a13">Why does multi-turn web GRPO need dynamic context rather than repeated single-turn answer training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Awebagent-r1">WebAgent-R1</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Virginia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Clicks, inputs, and navigation change page state. Later actions need the current page and relevant history. Full rollouts connect terminal success to generated actions, and dynamic retention limits HTML growth. Behavior cloning and initialization also shape exploration; a group-advantage formula is not complete web interaction training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After login, a changed page requires reading the new form. Repeated answers from the first screenshot cannot teach that transition.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.16421">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2505.16421-webagent-r1/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-be6d569f718d3a13">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:webagent-r1" data-paper-title="WebAgent-R1" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6a3db74d6fed501a">What training problems do behavior-cloning warm-up and subsequent M-GRPO address?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Awebagent-r1">WebAgent-R1</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Virginia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Warm-up establishes basic interaction and initialization. M-GRPO uses relative full-task success to optimize the policy. The stages have distinct supervision; a GRPO registry name cannot replace the paper&#x27;s behavior and long-CoT initialization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>First learn legal clicks and inputs, then improve long-horizon choices from task outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.16421">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2505.16421-webagent-r1/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6a3db74d6fed501a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:webagent-r1" data-paper-title="WebAgent-R1" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-856a46c9abd64eb7">How can compressed web state avoid treating old DOM as the current actionable page?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Awebagent-r1">WebAgent-R1</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Virginia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Bind each action to the then-current observation and compressed context; a fixed initial page cannot substitute for dynamic state. The mini-suite uses deterministic text observations with no real DOM effects or Qwen/Llama updates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A button ID may become invalid after navigation even if it appears in history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.16421">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2505.16421-webagent-r1/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-856a46c9abd64eb7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:gigpo" data-paper-title="GiGPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-gigpo-7fac2585" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-de70025cd20df8d7">Why does GiGPO need both macro trajectory advantage and micro step advantage?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agigpo">GiGPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Terminal outcomes summarize the trajectory but do not identify useful steps. GiGPO compares trajectories, then actions grouped by recurrent anchor state, and adds global and local credit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two trajectories can ultimately fail while one action from their shared intermediate state is more helpful.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.10978">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2505.10978-gigpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-de70025cd20df8d7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:gigpo" data-paper-title="GiGPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e6181f3487b83939">Why compare micro advantages among actions from the same recurrent anchor state?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agigpo">GiGPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Different states vary in available actions and remaining difficulty, confounding direct return comparisons. A shared anchor controls local conditions better. Micro credit complements trajectory-level macro advantage; stochastic continuation means differences are not noiseless causal effects or a replacement for terminal success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Compare looking for a key and pushing a locked door from the same point, not against a trajectory already at the goal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.10978">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2505.10978-gigpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e6181f3487b83939">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:gigpo" data-paper-title="GiGPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-951a8f0b5718b90f">How do same-anchor micro groups differ from ranking all steps together?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agigpo">GiGPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A shared state makes comparisons more comparable; mixing states confounds difficulty and consequences. Shared plan steps can be local proxies but do not establish identical underlying environment states.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A high return in an easy state should not be the same baseline for a difficult one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.10978">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2505.10978-gigpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-951a8f0b5718b90f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:gigpo" data-paper-title="GiGPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-57d3ee83ffa537e5">Why record anchor identity and the corresponding action with GiGPO micro advantage?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agigpo">GiGPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The mean comes from the same G(s_t), so wrong keys or mixed states change the baseline. Keep macro/micro logs, actual group membership, and state-proxy boundaries, not only combined advantage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two screens with the same title can have different task state and should not be merged by title alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.10978">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2505.10978-gigpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-57d3ee83ffa537e5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ragen" data-paper-title="RAGEN" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-ragen-2a3a9785" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ef11042a5e1ad9ea">Why does RAGEN monitor Echo Trap separately?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aragen">RAGEN</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Northwestern</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Multi-turn stochastic training can enter self-reinforcing repetition, with collapsed reward variance and gradient spikes. StarPO-S uses trajectory filtering, a critic baseline, and gradient/clipping stabilization rather than interpreting low variance as learning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A policy can consistently follow a failed path without any improvement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.20073">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2504.20073-ragen/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ef11042a5e1ad9ea">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ragen" data-paper-title="RAGEN" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-50b92779eb94d4cb">Why doesn&#x27;t collapsed reward variance necessarily mean stable task learning?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aragen">RAGEN</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Northwestern</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The policy may repeat failures or rigid behavior. Collapsed variance with gradient spikes signals Echo Trap risk. Trajectory filtering, a critic baseline, and decoupled clipping address data, estimates, and update stability separately. Real task performance is still required; low variance alone is not successful convergence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If all rollouts repeat one ineffective command, returns are zero with no variance. This is exploration collapse, not mature capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.20073">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2504.20073-ragen/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-50b92779eb94d4cb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ragen" data-paper-title="RAGEN" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3a4fb5b58a42b90f">How does StarPO-S trajectory filtering differ from clipping ratios only inside PPO loss?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aragen">RAGEN</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Northwestern</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Filtering controls which trajectories enter the objective. Ratio clipping limits drift for admitted samples, while the critic and gradient controls are separate. One clipping operation does not replace the complete stabilization chain.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Repeated low-information trajectories can still dominate training samples even if their ratios are clipped.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.20073">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2504.20073-ragen/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3a4fb5b58a42b90f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ragen" data-paper-title="RAGEN" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b358c5305dd0b789">Does a periodic local Echo Trap probe measure the paper&#x27;s training-collapse curve?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aragen">RAGEN</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Northwestern</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It makes a stability path observable. The policy selects among deterministic candidates and never updates LLM parameters. Distinguish probe triggers, actual gradients, and large-scale training curves; counts are not evidence of model collapse.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Checking every few rounds does not imply that the paper&#x27;s Echo Trap occurred in those rounds.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.20073">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2504.20073-ragen/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b358c5305dd0b789">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:deepresearcher" data-paper-title="DeepResearcher" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-deepresearcher-9b53178e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-88cf40121cb186e1">Why does DeepResearcher treat search, browsing, evidence, and answers as one trajectory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adeepresearcher">DeepResearcher</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · HKU</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Answers depend on how evidence is found and used, and final text alone obscures credit. Answer and citation rewards plus query cost balance quality and expense over the full search.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One useful browse can make the answer verifiable, beyond making its final sentence fluent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.03160">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2504.03160-deepresearcher/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-88cf40121cb186e1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:deepresearcher" data-paper-title="DeepResearcher" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-aff7e18e331cc491">Why isn&#x27;t citation count enough when adding citation rewards to answer rewards?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adeepresearcher">DeepResearcher</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · HKU</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Citations connect claims to real evidence, while counts can reward repeated or irrelevant links. Search, browsing, and answering form one trajectory. Joint objectives should enforce support and correctness while penalizing wasted queries. Check claim–source links; one browse call does not establish evidence use.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Ten irrelevant links should not beat two sources that directly support the conclusion, or the policy will learn link stuffing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.03160">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2504.03160-deepresearcher/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-aff7e18e331cc491">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:deepresearcher" data-paper-title="DeepResearcher" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4a779c50af1afc7e">Why aren&#x27;t citation quality rewards and query-count penalties the same efficiency objective?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adeepresearcher">DeepResearcher</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · HKU</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Citation reward measures evidential support; query penalty controls cost. Fewer searches do not ensure reliable evidence, and more citations do not ensure useful searches. The three weights govern trade-offs; short traces alone do not establish research quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Answering quickly after one bad query is cheap but unsupported.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.03160">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2504.03160-deepresearcher/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4a779c50af1afc7e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:deepresearcher" data-paper-title="DeepResearcher" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-fc41b0278af88bb1">How should DeepResearcher align citation rewards with actual retrieved evidence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adeepresearcher">DeepResearcher</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · HKU</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Citations must point to genuinely available material supporting corresponding statements, not just count as links. N_query counts actual search calls. The mini-suite has no real web or full LLM RL, so fixture citations are not external evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A title never retrieved and irrelevant to the claim should not receive credit for looking like a citation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.03160">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2504.03160-deepresearcher/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fc41b0278af88bb1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:search-r1" data-paper-title="Search-R1" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-search-r1-fce4d489" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-79676ef5125d404d">Why does Search-R1 repeatedly decide whether to search rather than using one-shot RAG?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asearch-r1">Search-R1</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Intermediate evidence can expose questions or revise a belief, requiring another query. Search is an environment; reasoning and search alternate, and final answer outcomes train the policy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A first retrieval reveals entity ambiguity, so the agent can query disambiguating conditions before answering.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.09516">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2503.09516-search-r1/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-79676ef5125d404d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:search-r1" data-paper-title="Search-R1" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c61b1b171492b766">Why mask retrieved tokens even though they occur in the input sequence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asearch-r1">Search-R1</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Search returns are environment output, not sampled policy actions. Policy loss there would teach the model to generate external evidence. Only its queries, reasoning, and answers are policy tokens; retrieval conditions later decisions. Iterative adaptation is not equivalent to a single static RAG retrieval.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A search result that says &#x27;published Tuesday&#x27; is not agent behavior. Train how to query and answer from evidence, not how to generate that environment text.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.09516">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2503.09516-search-r1/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c61b1b171492b766">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:search-r1" data-paper-title="Search-R1" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-38e311ec6e4bf35a">How does visible search context differ from training on retrieved text as policy-generated tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asearch-r1">Search-R1</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Documents can condition later actions, but their tokens come from the environment, not the policy. Mask their loss. Treating them as student outputs corrupts action probabilities for policy optimization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A thousand-character webpage does not count as a thousand-character agent action with policy gradients.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.09516">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2503.09516-search-r1/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-38e311ec6e4bf35a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:search-r1" data-paper-title="Search-R1" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7ba876b05ccaf382">How does Search-R1&#x27;s loss mask avoid masking the query action?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asearch-r1">Search-R1</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Separate model-generated reasoning and search instructions from environment information. The former remain policy tokens and the latter get mask zero. Use provenance boundaries, not a text match for &#x27;search.&#x27;</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The query inside `&lt;search&gt;` is an action; the following `&lt;information&gt;` text is an observation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.09516">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2503.09516-search-r1/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7ba876b05ccaf382">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:loop" data-paper-title="LOOP" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-loop-633efc7d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-65aace0802d88c38">Why does LOOP use several same-task trajectories instead of an independent value network?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aloop">LOOP</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apple</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Their returns provide a leave-one-out baseline without maintaining a critic. A PPO trust region supports reuse of expensive rollouts. Removing a value network does not remove importance ratios or drift control.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Compare one trajectory against the mean return of the other traces for its task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.01600">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2502.01600-loop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-65aace0802d88c38">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:loop" data-paper-title="LOOP" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-67c19d40e81f457a">Why exclude the current trajectory from its leave-one-out baseline?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aloop">LOOP</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apple</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Other group returns supply a critic-free reference without using the trajectory&#x27;s own reward in it. Long rollouts are expensive, making token-level ratio clipping and batch reuse useful, but repeated updates still face policy drift. Old trajectories do not become indefinitely fresh on-policy data.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>For rewards one, one, and zero, compare the first with the mean of the other two, then clip locally drifting tokens separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.01600">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2502.01600-loop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-67c19d40e81f457a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:loop" data-paper-title="LOOP" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1fab1e9ed3f8bc5a">How does LOOP token-level clipping differ from discarding a trajectory as soon as one token drifts?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aloop">LOOP</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apple</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local clipping constrains drift while retaining other useful parts of a long trace. Whole-trajectory dropping loses more expensive interaction data. Reuse must preserve old behavior probabilities; off-policy samples are not newly on-policy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One abnormal ratio in a hundred-step trajectory need not erase all other feedback.</p>
