<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.01600">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2502.01600-loop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1fab1e9ed3f8bc5a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:loop" data-paper-title="LOOP" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-725085d718d823b9">Can LOOP compute its leave-one-out baseline directly when K=1?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aloop">LOOP</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apple</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. K−1 is zero, so a singleton fails the group definition and needs explicit handling or rejection. Multi-epoch reuse must preserve the corresponding old policy probabilities and episode identity, not reinsert the sample&#x27;s own return into its baseline.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With one example, the mean of other examples does not exist.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.01600">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2502.01600-loop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-725085d718d823b9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>

<details class="ar-learning-guide" markdown="1"><summary>Topic guide and reading order</summary>

## Start with this question

If a long task gives only a terminal success or failure, which turn should receive credit?

## Takeaway

Connect actual environment trajectories to parameter updates. Agent Lightning separates execution from training so different frameworks can emit learnable transitions. GiGPO adds groups of revisited states for finer credit alongside trajectory-level information. World models, skill supervision, and interactive distillation also depend on state provenance. Distinguish student execution, expert demonstrations, and environment-model simulations.

## Example

A search task has query formulation, result reading, and submission. A wrong answer could follow an off-topic query or failure to use correct evidence. Multiple actions from the same intermediate state can support a fair comparison of outcomes. Grouping unrelated states by turn number confounds task difficulty and tool behavior with action value.

## Common pitfall

Step credit, policy updates, and capability are separate evidence levels. Finite gradients on synthetic states or three numerical seeds do not show browsing, programming, or exploration ability. A privileged training teacher or scorer may use hidden references, not the actor. Cost-based closure leaves component evidence at its original scope.

## Reading order

Read Agent Lightning for execution, transitions, and training, GiGPO for trajectory and step credit, and ASTEROID for distinguishing student context from teacher supervision across episodes in partially observed environments.

1. [Agent Lightning](../../../../agent-research/2508.03680-agent-lightning/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.03680)
2. [GiGPO](../../../../agent-research/2505.10978-gigpo/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.10978)
3. [Asymmetric On-Policy Distillation Learns In-Context Exploration](../../../../agent-research/2610.30105-asteroid/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30105v1)

## Check your understanding

Two third-turn actions look identical, but only one environment retrieved the right document. Can we group them for relative advantages?

??? note "Show suggested answer"

    Not by turn or text alone. Define and verify observable state and conditions that affect future returns. Otherwise advantage mixes environment differences. Keep execution failures and interrupted scoring to avoid selecting only successful trajectories.

</details>
